operations.specification: Validate guest sign-up or invitation-join credentials, create or resolve a guest identity as needed, and issue the initial JWT token set for temporary access. The implementation should accept the exact IErpHrmTimeGuest.IJoin contract, verify any required join token or invite payload, and persist a guest session record in the guest session store so the session can be refreshed later. Reject invalid, expired, or reused join data with a clear authentication error. Do not create any organization-scoped membership here unless the join payload explicitly represents that workflow in downstream business logic.
operations.description:
Creates or completes a guest access session for a visitor who is not yet authenticated. This endpoint is the guest entry point for the platform and returns the authorized token payload defined by IErpHrmTimeGuest.IAuthorized.

The operation supports the unauthenticated guest flow only. It is intended for temporary access before a user becomes a member account, and it should align with the guest session model by issuing a session that can be renewed later. Any token or invitation data supplied in the request must be validated before access is granted.

If the supplied join data is invalid, expired, or already consumed, the server should reject the request with an authentication error. No logout endpoint is required because guest access follows the same stateless JWT model as the rest of the authentication system.

requestBody.description: Guest join payload used to establish or complete a temporary authenticated guest session.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after a successful guest join.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate the refresh token or session renewal proof from an existing guest session, confirm that the session is still valid and unexpired, and issue a new JWT token set. The implementation should use the guest session store to verify the refresh context, rotate or extend session state according to security policy, and reject revoked, expired, or malformed refresh requests. Refresh should not create a new guest identity unless the refresh payload explicitly requires session rehydration.
operations.description:
Renews an existing guest authentication session and returns a fresh authorized token payload defined by IErpHrmTimeGuest.IAuthorized.

This endpoint exists so guests can continue using temporary platform access without re-running the initial join flow. It should rely on the guest session record as the source of truth for session validity and should issue new tokens only when the refresh credentials are accepted.

If the refresh token, session reference, or session state is invalid or expired, the request must fail with an authentication error. As with other JWT-based flows, no logout endpoint is needed; token expiration and client-side token disposal handle session termination.

requestBody.description: Guest refresh payload used to renew an existing temporary authentication session.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after a successful guest session refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Validate the member sign-up payload, create a new member account, and initialize the minimum authentication state needed for issuing tokens. The implementation should enforce email uniqueness, hash the password before persistence, and create any associated user identity records required by the platform. If the supplied email already exists but has pending organization invitations or pending memberships, the service should attach the new account to those pending organizations according to the registration rules. Return the authorized token payload only after the account creation transaction succeeds. Handle duplicate email, invalid password policy, and invitation/membership resolution failures with clear client errors.
operations.description:
Creates a new member account for the ERP HRM and time tracking platform. This operation is the registration entry point for users who sign up with email and password, and it returns the authenticated token payload after successful account creation.

The member account becomes the shared identity used across organizations, so the registration flow must preserve the user’s global profile and allow later organization membership linkage. If the email already has pending access to organizations, the registration process should connect the account to those pending memberships instead of creating duplicate access records.

If validation fails, the API should return a structured error response explaining the invalid email, password, or account state. If the email is already registered, the request must be rejected rather than creating a second account.

requestBody.description: Registration payload for creating a new member account with email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after successful member registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate the member login credentials, locate the matching account, and issue fresh authorization tokens when the password is correct. The implementation should verify the credential hash, reject inactive or blocked accounts if such states exist in the member schema, and record any session or security audit data supported by the authentication subsystem. If authentication succeeds, return the authorized token payload immediately. If credentials are invalid, respond with an authentication error without revealing whether the email exists.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing member using email and password and returns the token payload used to access organization-scoped APIs. This is the standard login operation for registered users of the ERP HRM and time tracking platform.

After successful authentication, the client can select an organization context and continue to use the same shared account across multiple organizations. The operation should not expose sensitive account state in failure responses, and it should treat unknown email addresses and invalid passwords uniformly.

If the member account is inactive or otherwise not eligible for login, the service should reject the request with an authorization error consistent with the account’s security state.

requestBody.description: Login payload containing the member email and password credentials.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the refresh token, confirm it belongs to a valid member session or token lineage, and issue a new authorized token payload. The implementation should enforce token rotation or replay protection if the session model supports it, and it should reject expired, revoked, or malformed refresh tokens. The operation must not require a password and should only renew authentication for an already recognized member identity. Return a standardized unauthorized error when the token is no longer valid.
operations.description:
Renews a member’s authentication state using a valid refresh token and returns a new authorized token payload. This keeps the user logged in across organization-scoped workflows without forcing repeated credential entry.

The refresh flow is part of the stateless JWT session lifecycle and should be used to obtain a new access token when the current one expires. It must preserve the member identity and continue to support subsequent organization context selection and secure access to the platform.

If the refresh token has expired, been revoked, or cannot be validated, the API must reject the request and require the client to sign in again.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload used to renew a member session.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after successful token renewal.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the current member's active and historical login sessions.

This operation returns session records that belong to the authenticated member account, including the client IP address, current entry URL, referrer URL, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. It is intended for account security review and session oversight, allowing the user to inspect where and when their account has been accessed.

The result set is scoped to the currently authenticated member only. The implementation must not expose sessions from other members, and it must support pagination, search, and sorting so the client can render manageable session history views. If the request asks for invalid page values or unsupported sort fields, the service should return a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_member_sessions for the authenticated member only.
Apply pagination, sorting, and optional text filtering against session context fields that are stored on the table, such as ip, href, and referrer.
Order results by created_at descending by default so the newest sessions appear first.
Return only the current member's rows; do not accept or use a member identifier in the request body because membership scope must come from the authenticated context.
If the current member is not available, reject the request as unauthorized.
If pagination values are out of range, reject with validation errors.
Use a lightweight summary projection suitable for lists, not the full member profile.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member session summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for the current member's session list.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single member session record.

This operation returns the full session details for a specific authenticated member session, including the owning member reference, captured IP address, request URL, referrer, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. It is intended for session inspection and security-related account management workflows.

The session record belongs to a member account and represents one issued login session. Consumers should treat the returned data as sensitive because it reflects active authentication context. If the session does not exist, the caller is not allowed to access it, or the session has already been removed, the server should respond with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the member session by its UUID primary key from erp_hrm_time_member_sessions.
Validate that sessionId is a UUID and fetch the record with its owning member relation if needed by the response serializer.
Enforce authorization so only the session owner or a privileged internal/admin workflow can read the record; otherwise return 403 or 404 according to the service’s security policy.
Do not expose any fields beyond the actual schema columns. Return 404 when the session record does not exist.

responseBody.description: Full member session details.

parameters.description: The member session identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's shared global profile.

This operation lets a user change the profile information that is visible across every organization they belong to. The shared profile includes display name, avatar image, and phone number, and the updated values must be reflected consistently wherever the member appears in the platform.

The update must apply only to the single global member profile stored on the member account. It must not create organization-specific profile data, and it must not modify authentication credentials or account lifecycle fields. Validation should reject any attempt to treat the profile as tenant-scoped or to write fields outside the shared profile attributes.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated member record and update only the shared profile fields on erp_hrm_time_members: display_name, avatar_image_url, and phone_number. Do not accept or persist email, password_hash, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, or id from the request body.

Validate that the request targets the current member account and that the profile remains global across all organizations. Persist the change in a single update statement and return the updated member representation. If the account cannot be resolved, return not found or unauthorized according to existing auth middleware behavior. If the input violates profile validation rules, reject with a validation error. Do not create any organization-specific profile records.

responseBody.description: The updated shared member profile after the change is applied.

requestBody.description: Fields used to update the authenticated member's shared global profile.

operations.description:
Update the settings of the currently selected organization.

This operation lets the organization owner maintain the tenant profile that defines the organization’s business identity and operating context. The editable settings include the organization name, description, logo image, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month, and the update applies only to the organization that is currently selected in the user’s context.

The endpoint is organization-scoped and owner-managed. The service must verify that the caller is working inside an active organization context and that the caller is the organization owner before persisting changes. If the organization cannot be resolved, if the caller lacks ownership, or if any value fails validation, the request must be rejected with an appropriate client error. The updated organization should be returned so the client can refresh its displayed tenant profile immediately.
operations.name: patch
operations.specification:
Resolve the currently selected organization from the authenticated member context, then verify the requester is the organization owner before applying changes. Load the organization record by the selected organization identifier, update only the editable organization profile columns present in the schema, and persist the changes in a single transaction.

Validate the submitted payload against the organization schema and business rules: reject missing or malformed values, reject attempts to modify fields outside the organization profile/settings scope, and ensure tenant isolation so only the selected organization is affected. If the organization is not found, return a not-found error. If the caller is not the owner, return a forbidden error. If the operation requires additional related settings rows in the schema, update them consistently within the same transaction.

Return the refreshed organization entity after update. Do not allow cross-organization updates, and do not infer or write fields that are not defined in the loaded organization schema.

responseBody.description: The updated organization after the settings change has been applied.

requestBody.description: Editable organization settings for the currently selected organization.

operations.description:
Create a new organization tenant for the ERP HRM and time tracking platform.

This operation creates the core organization record that defines an isolated business boundary for employees, projects, time tracking, and related organization-scoped data. The organization is owned by the creating member account, and the new tenant becomes available as an independent context for subsequent work.

The organization profile includes the organization name, optional description, optional logo image URL, and lifecycle state. The record is the root tenant entity, so validation should ensure the name is unique and the owner member reference is valid. Organization settings such as currency, timezone, and fiscal start month are managed separately in organization settings data and should not be duplicated here.

If creation fails, the service should return a validation or conflict error when the organization name already exists, or a not-found/authorization error when the owner member context is invalid. The created organization should be persisted together with its ownership reference and timestamps so that the new tenant is immediately usable in the selected organization context.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new record into erp_hrm_time_organizations with the owner member reference, organization name, optional description, optional logo image URL, and initial lifecycle status.

Validate that the owner member exists and is allowed to create the organization in the current authentication context. Enforce the unique organization name constraint before insert. Persist created_at and updated_at at creation time and leave deleted_at null.

Return the full created organization record after insert. Do not attempt to manage organization settings in this operation; those belong to the separate organization settings resource. If the unique name constraint is violated, respond with a conflict-style validation error. If the owner member context is invalid or missing, reject the request with an authorization or not-found error as appropriate.

responseBody.description: The newly created organization record.

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new organization tenant.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single organization by its identifier.

This endpoint returns the organization record that defines a tenant boundary for employees, projects, departments, roles, timelogs, timesheets, tasks, and activity log entries. It is intended for organization detail views, settings pages, and organization context checks in the authenticated member experience.

The returned organization must belong to the caller’s accessible scope. If the caller is not a member of the organization, or if the organization does not exist, the request must fail with the appropriate access or not-found error. The organization data is independent from other organizations and should be returned only for the currently authorized context.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization by its primary identifier within the authenticated user’s accessible organizations.
Verify that the caller has access to the organization through membership or ownership before returning the record.
Use a single read query against erp_hrm_time_organizations; include related settings only if they are part of the organization detail contract and exist in the schema. Do not expose data from other organizations.
Return a standard not-found error when the organization does not exist and a forbidden error when the caller lacks access.
If the endpoint is used by organization settings screens, ensure the response includes the fields required to render identity and configuration information for the active tenant boundary.

responseBody.description: The organization record for the requested tenant boundary.

parameters.description: The organization identifier in the current tenant scope.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Update an organization’s editable settings.

This operation lets an organization owner change the organization profile and operating context, including the name, description, logo image, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month. These values define how the tenant is identified and how business data is presented throughout the platform.

The update is applied only to the specified organization. It does not affect memberships, employees, projects, or data belonging to other organizations. Callers must be authorized in the selected organization context, and invalid values should be rejected with a clear validation error so the organization remains in a consistent state.
operations.name: putByOrganizationid
operations.specification:
Load the target organization by organizationId and verify the caller can manage organization settings in the selected organization context. Reject the request if the organization does not exist or if the caller lacks permission.

Apply only the editable organization fields from the update DTO: name, description, logo image, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month. Do not modify ownership, lifecycle state, memberships, employees, or other related tenant data.

Validate required business constraints on the updated values, especially acceptable currency, timezone, and fiscal month values. Persist the changes in a single transaction. If any rule fails, return a validation or authorization error and do not partially update the record.

responseBody.description: The updated organization record after the settings change has been saved.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization to update.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Editable organization settings to apply to the selected organization.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes an organization from the platform.

This operation is available to the organization owner while operating in the correct organization context. The organization must satisfy lifecycle safeguards before deletion is allowed: all pending timesheets must already be resolved, and there must be no active employee contracts. These checks protect unresolved work records and active employment arrangements from being removed prematurely.

When deletion succeeds, the organization is removed together with its organization-owned operational data, including employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets that belong to that organization. The owner’s account remains active, but it is no longer associated with the deleted organization. Any other organizations the owner belongs to are not affected.

If the organization still has unresolved timesheets or active contracts, the request must be rejected. If the caller is not authorized to manage the current organization context, the request must fail with an authorization error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the organization by organizationId within the caller's selected organization context and verify the caller has organization ownership/management rights for that tenant. Reject the request if the organization does not exist or does not belong to the current accessible context.

Before deletion, verify two hard constraints: (1) there are no pending timesheets for the organization, and (2) there are no active employee contracts. If either constraint is violated, return a conflict/validation error and do not modify data.

On success, delete the organization and all organization-owned dependent records that the domain rules require to be permanently deleted, including employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets. Ensure the deletion is executed transactionally so partial removal cannot occur. After the organization is deleted, preserve the owner account and remove its association with the deleted organization as required by the domain rules.

Do not expose or infer any soft-delete behavior. This is a permanent deletion workflow. Emit the appropriate activity/audit trail if the system records organization deletions elsewhere in the platform.

parameters.description: The organization identifier in the current tenant context.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Retrieve the settings record for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns the organization-scoped configuration that defines how the organization is represented and operated within the platform. The settings belong to the organization profile and must always be resolved through the requested organization context, so the result applies only to the specified organization.

Access is limited by the caller's organization context and permissions. If the organization cannot be found, if the caller is not allowed to access it, or if the settings record is unavailable for the organization, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization record by organizationId, then resolve its related organization_settings row through the 1:1 relation. If the organization does not exist, return a not-found error. If the caller is not allowed to access the organization context, return an authorization/context error. Because this is a read operation, do not modify any timestamps or settings values.

Select the settings row with currency_code, timezone, fiscal_start_month, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Since the settings table is a dependent extension of the organization, a missing settings row should be handled explicitly; either return not-found for the settings resource or materialize an error consistent with the rest of the service.

Do not include organization ownership or other organization fields in the settings response unless the shared DTO schema requires them. Keep the operation read-only and organization-scoped.

responseBody.description: The organization settings associated with the selected organization.

parameters.description: The organization identifier (UUID) for the organization whose settings are being retrieved.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Create or replace the settings record that defines an organization's operating context.

This operation stores the organization-wide currency, timezone, and fiscal start month for the selected organization. These values are part of the organization's business operating context and are maintained by the organization owner. The settings record is a dependent one-to-one extension of the organization record, so each organization can have at most one settings row.

The operation is restricted to the currently selected organization context and must only affect the organization identified by the path parameter. If the caller is not the organization owner, or if the organization context is missing or does not match the target organization, the request must be rejected. Validation must ensure the currency code, timezone, and fiscal start month are valid before persisting changes.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the organization by id and verify that it belongs to the active tenant context and that the authenticated member is the organization owner. Reject the request when no organization context is selected, when the target organization does not exist, or when ownership does not match.

Use the organization id to upsert the dependent erp_hrm_time_organization_settings row. If no settings row exists, create one; otherwise update the existing row. Persist only currency_code, timezone, and fiscal_start_month, and update timestamps through the normal persistence layer.

Validate currency_code as a supported ISO currency code, timezone as a valid IANA timezone identifier, and fiscal_start_month as an integer month in the range 1 to 12. If the parent organization is deleted, reject the operation. Preserve the one-to-one uniqueness constraint on erp_hrm_time_organization_id and return a conflict or validation error if another settings row would violate that constraint.

responseBody.description: The saved organization settings record containing the organization's operating context.

parameters.description: The identifier of the organization whose settings are being created or updated.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Organization operating-context settings to store for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Update the settings that define an organization's identity and operating context.

This operation lets the organization owner maintain the organization name, description, logo image, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month for the selected organization. These values form the shared business profile used by members of the organization for day-to-day work, reporting, and time-based calculations.

The update is scoped to a single organization and must not affect any other organization the caller may belong to. Only the organization owner is allowed to perform this action, and the server must reject requests that are missing organization context, reference the wrong organization, or attempt to modify settings without ownership.

Validation errors are returned when the supplied settings are incomplete or invalid, including invalid currency values, unsupported timezone values, or an out-of-range fiscal start month. The response returns the updated organization settings after persistence so clients can immediately reflect the new operating context.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the organization settings row for the given organizationId and verify it belongs to the same organization as the authenticated member's active organization context.

Authorize only the organization owner. Reject the request with a forbidden error if the caller is not the owner, and reject with a context error if no organization is currently selected or if the requested organization does not match the active context.

Validate the request body against the organization settings update contract. Enforce field-level checks for name, optional description, optional logo image URI, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month. Persist only the provided editable settings for that organization; do not touch other organizations or unrelated data.

Return the updated organization settings entity. If the organization cannot be found, return not found. If validation fails, return a structured validation error response. If the caller tries to update a non-owner-managed organization, return forbidden.

responseBody.description: The updated organization settings record after the changes are saved.

parameters.description: The organization identifier in the URL path (UUID scope).

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of organization memberships for a single organization.

This operation lets authorized users inspect the participation records that connect member accounts to the selected organization. Each result represents one membership and reflects the organization-specific role and membership status used to determine access within that tenant.

The list is always scoped to the organization identified in the path. This is important because a user may belong to multiple organizations, and membership data must never be mixed across tenants. Consumers can use this endpoint to browse members, review roles, and inspect whether a membership is active in the current organization context.

If the caller does not have access to the organization, the request must be rejected. If the organization does not exist, the service must return a not-found response. Filtering and pagination should follow the platform’s standard list behavior for organization-scoped resources.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query organization memberships for the given organization ID only.
Use the organization ID from the path as the mandatory tenant scope and do not allow cross-organization leakage.
Apply request-body filters for membership status, role, member identity, search text, pagination, and sorting as supported by the shared list contract.
Join or preload the linked member account and organization-specific role as needed to build summary rows.
Validate that the caller is authorized to view memberships in this organization, typically through organization access and the relevant member/organization permissions.
Return a paginated result set using the standard page wrapper for summary records.
Handle missing organization with 404, unauthorized access with 403, and invalid pagination/filter input with 400.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization membership summaries for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of organization memberships for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns membership records that connect user accounts to the active organization context, including the membership's role and status. It is intended for organization-level member management and browsing, where access is evaluated only within the current organization selected by the signed-in user.

The result set is scoped to the active organization and must not include memberships from other organizations. Consumers may filter and sort the list to support member administration screens, role reviews, and status-based browsing. Authorization should require organization-scoped access, and callers without access to the active organization must be rejected.

Validation and error handling should enforce that pagination values are valid, filters are well-formed, and the selected organization context belongs to the authenticated member. If the current session has no valid organization context, or if the caller lacks permission to view memberships in that organization, the request must fail with an authorization error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement as a membership search endpoint scoped to the authenticated user's selected organization context.

Query erp_hrm_time_organization_memberships using the active organization identifier from session/context, never from client-supplied body fields. Apply filters for membership status, role, and member search criteria. Join to the member table only as needed for name/email display and to resolve membership ownership details for summaries.

Support pagination, sorting, and stable ordering. Default ordering should prioritize the selected-organization membership list UX, typically by member display name or creation order if present in schema. Ensure the response excludes memberships from other organizations even if the same user has multiple memberships elsewhere.

Enforce authorization before querying: callers must have permission to view members in the active organization. Return forbidden if the user is outside the organization or lacks member-view privileges. Validate all paging parameters and reject invalid filter values. If the selected organization context is missing or no longer corresponds to one of the user's memberships, return a context error.

Return paginated summary rows rather than full nested entities to keep the list efficient. Include enough information for administrative member tables, especially membership identity, linked member identity, role, and status. Do not allow the request body to override organization scope.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization membership summaries for the active organization context.

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, and filter criteria for browsing memberships within the selected organization context.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single organization membership for the selected organization context.

An organization membership represents the business link between a user account and one organization. It carries the organization-scoped role and membership status that determine whether the member currently has access inside that organization.

Use this operation when viewing membership details for administration, role assignment review, or access checks. The returned membership reflects the current organization context, so the caller can only inspect membership data within the organization they are working in.

If the membership does not exist in the selected organization context, or if the caller is not allowed to view organization membership data, the server must return the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization membership by its identifier, but always enforce the currently selected organization context from the authenticated member session. Query erp_hrm_time_organization_memberships by primary identifier and organization scope; reject access if the record belongs to a different organization than the active context.

Return the full membership entity needed for detail views, including the linked user account reference, organization reference, assigned role, membership status, and selected organization context fields that exist in the schema. Do not expose memberships across organizations even if the same user belongs to multiple organizations.

Handle missing records with a not-found response. Handle authorization failures when the caller lacks permission to view organization membership information in the active organization. Do not mutate data in this operation.

responseBody.description: The organization membership record for the selected organization context.

operations.description:
Update an organization membership record.

This operation modifies the membership link between a member account and an organization. The membership stores the organization-scoped access association, the current membership status, and whether this membership is the member's selected organization context.

Use this endpoint to change the membership status or selected-context flag for the specified membership. The system must preserve the uniqueness of the member-and-organization pair, and it must keep organization access isolated to the current organization context. If the membership does not exist, the request must fail with a not-found error. If the update would violate membership rules or organization context constraints, the request must be rejected with a validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the organization membership by its UUID and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization context before applying updates. Allow updates only to fields supported by the membership update DTO, such as status and selected-context flag, and never allow modification of the member or organization foreign keys through this endpoint.

Enforce the existing unique member-and-organization constraint at save time. When setting a membership as the selected context, clear the selected-context flag from other memberships of the same member so that only one organization context remains active at a time. Preserve all audit timestamps, updating updated_at on success. If the requested status is not allowed by business rules, or if the update targets a membership outside the active organization scope, return a validation or authorization error as appropriate.

responseBody.description: The updated organization membership record after the changes are applied.

parameters.description: The organization membership identifier (UUID) to update.
parameters.name: organizationMembershipId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of employees for the current organization context.

This endpoint supports browsing the organization’s employee directory, which is used to find staff records and review summary information. Users can search by employee name and filter the list by department, employment type, and status, while the results remain limited to the currently selected organization.

Access depends on the caller’s employee-view permission within the active organization context. The response returns summary data intended for directory and table views, and the system must keep pagination stable so users can move through pages without losing the current search and filter selections. Requests with invalid filter values or pagination settings should be rejected with validation errors.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read employee records from erp_hrm_time_employees within the active organization context only.
Join against related lookup data as needed for summary fields such as department and role, but do not leak cross-organization rows.
Apply request filters for department, employment type, status, and case-insensitive name search. Support stable sorting and pagination in the list query; default ordering should be deterministic for repeatable pages.
Return a paginated summary payload using the service’s standard page contract.
Validate that department filters belong to the current organization and that employment type/status values are among the allowed enum values from the employee domain. Reject invalid pagination or sort inputs with a 400-style validation error. If the caller lacks permission to view employee lists in the current organization, return a forbidden error. If the organization context is missing or invalid, return an organization-context error.

responseBody.description: Paginated employee summaries for the selected organization context.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for browsing employees in the active organization.

prerequisites.description: A department must exist in the selected organization before a departmentId filter can be used to browse employees by department.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single employee record for the currently selected organization context.

This operation returns the employee profile used for human resource administration and employee detail screens. It is scoped to the active organization, so the employee must belong to that organization before the record can be returned. The employee record represents a user account’s participation in a specific organization and includes the employee’s role assignment, department, employment type, and status.

Access is restricted to users with employee visibility permission or stronger organization management privileges. The response is intended for employee detail views and related workflows such as role assignment review, department grouping, and employment status management. If the employee does not exist in the current organization context, the request must fail with a not-found error; if the caller lacks permission, it must fail with an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the employee by employeeId with a query constrained to the current organization context from the authenticated member session.
Join or load the employee’s role and optional department only if the API response schema requires nested references; otherwise return the persisted employee entity fields directly.
Validate that the resolved employee belongs to the selected organization before returning data. Reject the request with 404 if no employee exists in the current organization, even if the identifier exists in another tenant.
Enforce permission checks before data retrieval or before response serialization: callers must have employee:view permission, with employee:manage or org:manage also allowed through role-based access.
Do not expose employees from other organizations or any cross-tenant references. Preserve the employee’s status, role, department, and employment type exactly as stored. No mutation occurs in this operation.

operations.description:
Update an employee record within the current organization.

This operation allows authorized users to maintain an employee’s organization-scoped employment details, including department assignment, position or title, employment type, role, and status. An employee belongs to one user account and one organization, and exactly one role must always be assigned within that organization.

The employee record is used for staff grouping, access control, and human resources management. Department assignment is optional, but when present it must reference an existing department in the same organization. If the department has been removed, the employee’s department reference is cleared rather than moving the employee to another organization. Deactivating an employee preserves historical timelogs, timesheets, and contracts, while preventing new time tracking actions until the employee is reactivated.

Only users with employee management permission may perform this update. The service must validate organization scope from the authenticated context, reject cross-organization access, and return clear validation errors when the employee does not exist, the referenced role or department is invalid, or the requested status change conflicts with business rules.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the employee by employeeId within the authenticated organization scope. Reject the request with not found if the employee does not belong to the current organization.

Apply only mutable employee fields from IErpHrmTimeEmployee.IUpdate. Support updates for department, position/title, employment type, role assignment, and status-related fields as allowed by the underlying schema and business rules. Do not allow changing the organization or user-account ownership of the employee through this endpoint.

Validate that any supplied department belongs to the same organization and exists. If the department is missing or deleted, clear the department reference only when the request explicitly indicates removal; otherwise reject invalid references. Validate that the assigned role belongs to the same organization and that exactly one role remains assigned after the update.

If status is changed to deactivated, enforce the rule that the employee cannot be left in a state that would break historical records; existing timelogs, timesheets, and contracts remain untouched. If reactivating, simply persist the status change and do not recreate any memberships or contracts automatically.

Use a transaction for updates that touch multiple relational fields. If the schema includes audit-related write hooks, they may emit activity log entries outside this endpoint; otherwise do not fabricate activity records here. Return the updated employee entity after persistence.

Common errors: 404 when the employee does not exist in scope; 400 for invalid department, role, or employment type; 403 when the caller lacks employee management permission; 409 when a requested change violates organization rules or uniqueness constraints.

operations.description:
Retrieve the contract history for a specific employee.

This operation returns the employee’s employment contracts in historical order so callers can review how compensation and working arrangements changed over time. It is intended for employee self-service and for users who have employee view permission within the organization.

The contract records are organization-scoped through the employee relationship and represent historical employment terms such as start date, optional end date, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, and notes. Past contracts remain immutable, while the current active contract is the only contract that may be changed through a separate update operation.

If the employee does not exist, the caller does not have access to the employee, or the organization context does not match, the request must be rejected. The response is paginated to support employees with long contract histories.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target employee by employeeId within the current organization context, then verify the caller can view that employee's contracts. Allow self-access for the authenticated employee and allow cross-employee access only when the caller has employee:view permission.

Query erp_hrm_time_employee_contracts filtered by erp_hrm_time_employee_id, ordered chronologically by start_date ascending (and created_at or id as a stable tie-breaker if needed). Return a paginated result set of contract summaries for list display. Include the contract fields needed for history browsing and current-state review, but do not expose any mutation behavior here.

Support search/pagination criteria in the request body. If the employee has no contracts, return an empty page. If the employee id is invalid or does not belong to the current organization context, return a not-found or forbidden error according to existing authorization conventions. Do not attempt to modify contracts from this endpoint; past contracts are immutable and active-contract editing is handled elsewhere.

operations.description:
Create a new employment contract for an employee.

This operation adds a new contract record to the employee's historical employment record within the current organization context. A contract captures the employee's start date, optional end date, compensation terms, weekly working-hour expectation, and optional notes. The employee is identified by the path parameter, and the new contract is always created in the scope of that employee.

When a new contract is created, the system must close the previous active contract for the same employee by setting its end date to the day before the new contract starts. This preserves a continuous employment history and ensures that only one active contract exists at a time. Past contracts remain immutable historical records after they are no longer active.

Access is restricted to users who are allowed to manage employee data or view contract records according to organization permissions. The system must reject attempts to create overlapping active contracts, invalid pay periods, or contract data that does not satisfy the required dates and compensation terms. Because contracts belong to employees, all reads and writes must remain isolated to the current organization.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target employee by employeeId within the current organization context and verify the caller has employee management access for contract creation. Reject the request if the employee does not exist, belongs to another organization, or is inaccessible in the current tenant scope.

Validate the payload using the actual contract fields only: startDate, endDate, payRate, payPeriod, workingHoursPerWeek, and notes. Enforce that startDate and payRate are present, payPeriod is one of hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, and workingHoursPerWeek is provided. Reject invalid date ordering where endDate exists and is before startDate. Because the schema exposes deleted_at but business rules treat contracts as historical records, do not expose any manual delete behavior here.

Before inserting the new row, find the current active contract for the same employee using the existing date-range rules and close it by setting its endDate to the day before the new startDate. Perform this in a transaction so the update of the previous active contract and insertion of the new contract are atomic. If a contract with the same employee and startDate already exists, return a validation conflict based on the unique constraint.

Persist the new contract row with the employee foreign key from the path and audit timestamps. Return the created contract entity. If business rules or persistence checks fail, surface a clear domain validation error rather than partially updating the employee's history.

responseBody.description: The newly created employee contract record, including its persisted dates, compensation terms, and timestamps.

Retrieve a single employee contract record for viewing contract history.

This operation returns one historical employment contract belonging to a specific employee within the current organization context. The contract contains the employee’s effective date range, compensation terms, working-time expectations, and optional notes, allowing consumers to review how the employee’s employment arrangement was defined at that point in time.

The contract is part of an employee’s immutable history. Consumers can use this endpoint to inspect the active or past contract details for the employee, while authorization rules ensure that employees may view their own contracts and users with employee view permission may view any employee’s contracts in the organization. The employee relationship is organization-scoped, so the request must be validated against both the employee and contract identifiers before returning data.

If the employee does not exist in the current organization, the contract does not belong to that employee, or the caller lacks permission to view the record, the request must be rejected with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.

Load the employee record by employeeId within the current organization context, then load the contract by contractId constrained to that employeeId. Do not allow cross-employee access: the contract must belong to the same employee referenced in the path. Because both ids are UUID primary keys, validate them as UUID path parameters.

Return the full contract entity with all persisted fields: id, employee reference, start date, end date, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, notes, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at if present in the persisted record. Do not fabricate any derived fields.

Enforce authorization using the organization-scoped employee view rule: the caller may read their own contract history, or must have employee:view permission to read another employee’s contracts. Reject requests outside the current organization context. If the employee-contract relation is missing, return not found rather than exposing whether the contract exists globally. Because this is a historical record, no mutation logic is involved.

operations.description:
Update the current active contract for an employee.

This operation lets authorized users change the active employment terms for a specific employee within the currently selected organization. The contract record is part of the employee’s historical employment record, so the API must preserve past contracts and only allow editing when the target contract is still the active one.

The contract stores the employee reference, effective dates, compensation terms, pay period, weekly working hours, and optional notes. When the updated contract affects the active period, the service must validate the date range, ensure the employee belongs to the current organization, and reject attempts to modify past contracts. If the caller does not have employee-view access for the target employee, the request must be denied.

If the update changes the contract start date while preserving it as the active contract, the implementation must ensure the employee still has at most one active contract and must prevent overlaps with other contracts. Validation errors should be returned for invalid dates, unsupported pay periods, missing required contract fields, or attempts to edit an immutable historical contract.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target employee and contract within the current organization context using both path identifiers. Verify the employee exists, belongs to the selected organization, and the contract belongs to that employee. Enforce authorization: the caller may update their own active contract only if permitted by the business rules, while updating another employee’s contract requires employee manage permission; if access is only through viewing, reject with a permission error.

Confirm the contract is the active contract before applying changes. Past contracts must not be modified. Validate all incoming fields against the schema and business rules: start date is required, pay rate is required, pay period must be one of hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, working hours per week are required, notes are optional, and end date may be null. Reject updates that would create overlapping active periods or violate the one-active-contract rule.

Use a transaction when persisting updates so the employee’s contract history remains consistent. If the contract start date or end date changes, re-evaluate whether the contract remains active and whether surrounding contract dates still form a continuous history. Do not auto-edit older contracts unless required by a direct contract-rollover workflow; this endpoint should only update the addressed contract.

Return the updated contract entity after persistence. If the contract cannot be found, return a not-found error. If the contract is not active, return a validation or conflict error indicating the record is immutable. If organization context is missing or mismatched, reject the request as unauthorized or forbidden.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of departments for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is used to browse the organization’s internal department structure, including parent-child relationships and department descriptions. Employees can use it to understand how the organization is grouped, while users with management permission can use the same list to locate departments for editing or deletion.

The result is restricted to the active organization context. Departments from other organizations must never be returned. The list should honor the current hierarchy and exclude records that are not visible according to the organization’s department browsing rules. Search, filtering, pagination, and sorting should be supported for department name, parent department, and deletion state where applicable.

If the organization context is missing or invalid, or if the caller attempts to browse outside the selected organization, the request must be rejected. The operation must respect the unique department naming rule within an organization and avoid exposing duplicate or cross-tenant department data.
operations.name: index

Query erp_hrm_time_departments using the selected organization context from the authentication/session layer.
Apply a mandatory filter on erp_hrm_time_organization_id to enforce tenant isolation.
Support pagination, free-text search on name, and optional filtering by parent department and deleted state if the request DTO includes those controls. Sort results deterministically, preferably by name and then created_at for stable paging.

Return summary rows only, not full relationship graphs, to keep the list lightweight. Include parent department identifiers or summary references only if the summary schema supports them. Do not join across organizations. If the search term matches no rows, return an empty page rather than an error.

Because the schema defines @@unique([erp_hrm_time_organization_id, name]), treat department names as organization-scoped. Do not attempt to infer or expose duplicate structures across tenants. Use the existing deleted_at column only for filtering if the list is meant to show archived/removed departments; otherwise, return active records according to the business browsing rule. If the caller lacks access to the selected organization, reject the request as unauthorized/forbidden.

operations.description:
Create a department for the currently selected organization.

Departments are organizational groupings used to organize employees and describe the organization’s internal structure. This operation lets organization managers add a new department with a name, an optional description, and an optional parent department so the organization can represent a simple one-level hierarchy.

The department belongs only to the active organization context. The parent department, if provided, must also belong to the same organization and must not create a deeper hierarchy. If the request would create a duplicate or unclear department structure, the request is rejected. Employees can view departments through read operations, but only users with organization management permission can create them.
operations.name: create

Insert a new record into erp_hrm_time_departments using the currently selected organization context as the owning scope.

Validate that the caller has organization management permission. Require a department name. Accept an optional description and optional parent department reference. If a parent is supplied, verify that it exists, belongs to the same organization, and does not violate the single-level hierarchy rule.

Before inserting, check for duplicate or conflicting department structures within the same organization, including cases where the same name/parent combination would create an ambiguous structure. Reject the request if the target organization context is missing or if the parent belongs to another organization.

Return the created department after persistence. If the underlying schema uses an organization foreign key or parent foreign key, populate them from context and validated input only. Do not modify employees here; employee department clearing is handled by delete operations elsewhere.

The returned department must belong to the active organization context. If the department does not exist in the selected organization, the request must be rejected. The response is intended for both management screens and read-only employee views that need to show the organizational structure.

Departments are organization-scoped structural labels used to organize employees and reflect the internal hierarchy of the organization. This operation lets authorized users change the department name, description, and parent department while preserving the department's identity and organization ownership.

The department hierarchy is limited to one level of nesting. The parent department, when provided, must belong to the same organization and must not create deeper nesting or a duplicate/confusing structure. Department names must remain unique within the organization.

If a department is removed elsewhere in the system, employees assigned to it are cleared from that department rather than being deleted. This update operation must reject requests that target a department outside the currently selected organization or that would violate department uniqueness or hierarchy rules.
operations.name: update

Load the target department by id and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization. Reject the request if the department does not exist, is deleted, or is outside the selected organization context.

Validate mutable fields from IErpHrmTimeDepartment.IUpdate: name, description, and parentDepartmentId (or equivalent parent reference defined by the DTO). Reject updates that would create duplicate or confusing department structures within the same organization.

When a parent department is supplied, verify the parent belongs to the same organization, is not the same department, and does not introduce nesting deeper than one level. Since the schema is self-referential, prevent cycles and multi-level chains by ensuring the chosen parent has no parent of its own if the business rule requires a strict one-level tree.

Permanently removes a department from the selected organization.

When a department is deleted, any employees assigned to that department keep their employee records, but their department assignment is cleared so that historical employee data remains intact.

The deletion is limited to the current organization context and does not affect departments in other organizations. Clients should expect permission checks and validation failures when the department does not exist, is outside the current organization, or the caller lacks organization management permission.

Before deleting the department row, query employees referencing this department and update those employee records so their department reference becomes null. Preserve all employee records and do not cascade-delete employees.

Delete the department record in the same transaction after clearing employee assignments. Ensure the operation respects the one-level department hierarchy: deleting a parent department removes that department only, while the employees linked to it are disassociated. Return an error if the caller lacks access or if the department cannot be deleted due to domain constraints enforced by persistence rules.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of roles for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns both built-in and custom roles that belong to the active organization context. Roles are organization-specific, so the result is always scoped to the user’s selected organization and never crosses tenant boundaries. The list is intended for role management screens where owners and other authorized members need to browse role names, descriptions, built-in status, and related permission sets.

The response is optimized for pagination and search. Consumers can filter roles by built-in status and search by role name or description to find the relevant role quickly. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee remain part of the organization’s baseline access model and are included in the list, while custom roles reflect organization-defined access responsibility.

If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks permission to view roles, the request must be rejected. The service must also ensure that only roles belonging to the active organization are returned, and it should not expose permission catalog records directly except through the role’s assigned permission summary.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the active organization from the authenticated member context and query erp_hrm_time_roles by erp_hrm_time_organization_id. Support pagination, sorting, and search terms in the request body. Search should match role name and optional description. Allow filtering by built-in status and, if supported by the DTO, by assigned permission keys through joins to erp_hrm_time_role_permissions and erp_hrm_time_permissions.

Always exclude roles from other organizations. Use a count query for pagination metadata and return role summaries only, not the full normalized permission join rows. Preserve stable ordering when multiple sort keys are provided. If the organization context is absent, return a context/authorization error. If the caller lacks role-view access according to the organization permission model, deny the request.

operations.description:
Create a new role within the currently selected organization.

This operation creates an organization-scoped role record for the active tenant context. The caller must have the appropriate role-management permission in the selected organization, and the role name must be unique within that organization.

If the request includes approved permissions, the system stores the role and its permission assignments together so the resulting role can be used immediately for membership-based access control in that organization. Validation errors are returned when the organization context is missing, the caller is not allowed to manage roles, the role name already exists, or any requested permission is not part of the approved permission catalog.

Insert a new record into erp_hrm_time_roles using the current organization context and validate that the caller has organization owner or equivalent role-management permission. Enforce uniqueness of (erp_hrm_time_organization_id, name) before insert. Reject attempts to create built-in roles through this endpoint unless the business layer explicitly permits system-seeded bootstrap data; normal API usage should create custom roles only.

If permissions are included in the request, validate every requested permission against erp_hrm_time_permissions by key or identifier, then create erp_hrm_time_role_permissions rows for each approved permission in the same transaction as the role insert. Roll back the entire transaction if any permission is invalid or any insert fails.

Return the created role entity after persistence. Ensure the response reflects the organization-scoped role record and, if the component schema includes nested permissions, populate them from the join table. Do not allow cross-organization role creation, and do not accept any organization identifier from the request body if the current organization context already determines scope.

Retrieve a single organization role in the current organization context.

If the role is not found in the current organization context, the server must return a not-found error. If the caller does not have permission to view role data, the request must be rejected according to the organization access rules.

Load the role by `id` within the current organization context and ensure the row belongs to the active organization. Use a single indexed lookup by primary key, then verify `erp_hrm_time_organization_id` matches the request context to prevent cross-tenant access.

The `is_builtin` flag must be preserved so downstream consumers can distinguish protected baseline roles from editable custom roles.

Handle not-found and unauthorized cases explicitly. If the role exists but belongs to a different organization, respond as not found to avoid tenant leakage. No mutation or side effects occur in this operation.

Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are part of the organization’s fixed access model and must remain unchanged. The service must verify that the target role belongs to the current organization, enforce role-edit permissions, and reject requests that attempt to modify immutable built-in roles or permissions outside the approved catalog.

Return 409 or 422 if the update would violate role rules, such as attempting to edit an immutable built-in role or assigning unsupported permissions. The returned permission records represent the fixed business abilities used across the ERP HRM and time tracking platform, including organization management, employee management and viewing, project management and viewing, time management, time approval, viewing all time records, and report viewing. These records are reference data and are not created or edited through this API.

Access to this endpoint follows the organization’s active context and the caller’s authorization rules. If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks permission to manage or inspect role configuration, the request should be rejected. Filtering, pagination, and sorting should be applied consistently so the permission catalog can be reused in UI role selectors and admin tools.

Read the approved permission catalog from erp_hrm_time_permissions.

Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request body to satisfy the index contract. Search should match permission code/name/description fields exposed by the schema. Sorting should allow stable ordering, defaulting to a deterministic field such as name or code if present in the schema; do not assume fields that do not exist.
Return only permissions from the approved list used for custom roles. Do not expose any mechanism to create, update, or delete permissions. The permission record is identified by its UUID primary key. If the permission does not exist, the server must return a not-found error. Because this endpoint reads from the global approved permission catalog, it does not depend on organization context and does not accept a request body.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load a single row from erp_hrm_time_permissions by id using the UUID path parameter.
Return the permission only if it exists and is not deleted_at-marked inactive; otherwise return not found.
Do not join to other tables because the permission catalog is self-contained.
The endpoint is read-only and must not require organization context.
Keep the response stable for role-editing workflows by returning the canonical permission entity fields only.

operations.description:
Assign an approved permission to a role within the selected organization.

This operation adds one permission to the specified role and is intended for organization role administration. Roles are organization-scoped, and the permission being attached must come from the platform's approved permission catalog. Built-in roles and custom roles share the same assignment model, but the caller must still respect organization ownership and access-control rules.

The created association is stored through the role-permission relation, which links a role record to an approved permission record. Duplicate assignments are rejected, and permissions outside the approved list are not allowed. If the role does not belong to the current organization, or if the caller lacks permission to manage roles, the request must fail with an authorization or validation error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the role by roleId and verify it belongs to the current organization context. Require permission-management authorization according to the selected organization's access rules, typically owner-level role administration.

Validate that the requested permission exists in the approved permission catalog and is not deleted. Reject the request if the permission key is not one of the approved organization permissions. Resolve the permission by key or identifier as defined by the create DTO, then insert a row into erp_hrm_time_role_permissions with the role id and permission id.

Prevent duplicates by checking the unique pair (erp_hrm_time_role_id, erp_hrm_time_permission_id). If the pair already exists, return a conflict-style validation failure. Use a transaction so concurrent requests cannot create duplicate role-permission rows. Return the newly created relation with its linked role and permission references if the API contract expects a full object.

operations.description:
Update the permission set assigned to a role within the currently selected organization.

This operation lets an organization owner or another authorized member with role-management capability change what a role can do. It applies to organization-scoped roles and enforces the approved permission catalog so that only valid business permissions can be attached to a role.

Built-in roles remain governed by the organization’s access model, while custom roles can be adjusted to match the organization’s current structure. The system validates the requested permissions, rejects any value outside the approved list, and preserves the role’s organization scope. If the role is currently assigned to employees, the update affects their access immediately within the selected organization.

If the role cannot be found in the active organization, the request fails with a not-found error. If the caller lacks authorization, the request fails with an access error. If the permission set contains invalid or unsupported entries, the request fails with a validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId and ensure it belongs to the current organization context. Verify the caller is authorized to manage roles and permission assignments according to organization access rules.

Accept a request body containing the full desired permission set for the role. Validate each permission against the approved permission catalog; reject any permission outside the allowed list. Preserve the role identity, name, organization, and built-in/custom classification; only modify the permission assignment data.

If the role is built-in, enforce any schema or business constraints that prevent unsupported permission changes. If the role is custom, update the stored permission set atomically so that concurrent edits cannot partially apply. Return the updated role permissions after persistence.

Handle errors explicitly: return not found when the role does not exist in the current organization, forbidden when the caller cannot manage roles, and bad request when the permission set is missing, empty when not allowed, duplicated, or contains unsupported values. Record any required audit/activity entry if the service layer uses activity logging for role changes.

responseBody.description: The role after its permission set has been updated.

operations.description:
Remove a permission assignment from a role.

This operation permanently removes a single permission link from an organization role. It is used when an organization owner edits a custom role's access set and no longer wants that permission attached to the role.

The role context is required because permissions belong to a specific role within the organization. The target permission assignment must exist under the given role, and the server should reject the request if the association does not belong to that role or if the role cannot be modified by the current member.

Built-in roles are protected by role business rules, so the service must prevent modifications that would violate the organization access model. If the role-permission assignment cannot be found, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks role management authority, return a forbidden error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the role by roleId within the current organization context and verify the caller has permission to manage roles. Then load the role-permission association by rolePermissionId constrained to the same role. Reject the request if the association does not belong to the specified role or if the role is built-in and protected by business rules that forbid modifying its permission set in this way.

Delete the role-permission row in a transaction. No cascading delete should be needed beyond removing the association record itself. If the schema uses organization-scoped role ownership, ensure the role also belongs to the active organization before deleting. Return not found when either the role or the association does not exist in scope, and return forbidden when the caller lacks access. Do not expose any response payload.
