operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of projects within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is used to browse project records that belong to the active organization context. It supports filtering and sorting so users can quickly find projects by status or other list criteria, while preserving strict tenant isolation between organizations.

Access is limited to members who have permission to view projects in the selected organization. The response is intended for project overviews and list pages, and includes summary data suitable for displaying project identity and status in UI tables or cards.

If the caller does not have project view permission, the request must be rejected. If the selected organization context is missing or invalid, the request must also be rejected. Results must never include projects from another organization.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read projects from erp_hrm_time_projects constrained to the current organization context from the authenticated member session. Apply permission checks for project:view before querying.

Support pagination, keyword search, status filtering, and stable sorting in the request body. Every query must be scoped by organization id, and any status filter must not cross tenant boundaries. Return only summary fields needed for browsing, including project identity, display metadata, and lifecycle status.

Sort by a deterministic default when the client does not specify sort order. Reject requests with invalid filters, unsupported sort fields, or missing organization context. If the underlying project schema includes visual distinction data such as color, include it in summary projection if available. Use a paginated response DTO named IPageIErpHrmTimeProject.ISummary.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summaries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for browsing projects in the current organization.

operations.description:
Create a new project in the current organization.

This operation allows authorized users to register a project that will be used for planning, task management, and time tracking. The project belongs to the currently selected organization and must be created with a valid display color so it can be visually distinguished in project lists and work views.

Projects are organization-scoped records. The created project can later be assigned employees through project memberships, receive tasks, and accumulate timelog entries. The status, budget, and schedule fields define the project’s operational state and planning context. If the caller does not have permission to manage projects, the request must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the caller has project management permission in the current organization context.
Insert a new row into erp_hrm_time_projects using the selected organization scope and the submitted project attributes.
Enforce required field validation for the project identity and visual color code, and validate any status or date fields according to the project business rules.
Prevent cross-organization creation by binding the record to the active organization only; never accept an organization identifier from the client body.
Return the newly created project entity after persistence. If downstream rules reject the project state or required fields are invalid, surface a validation error. If authorization is missing, return a forbidden response.

responseBody.description: The newly created project record.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project within the currently selected organization.

This operation returns the full project record for viewing project details, including the project’s identity, display metadata, lifecycle status, schedule, and budget information. It is intended for project detail screens and other workflows that need the complete project entity rather than a list summary.

Access is limited to users who can view projects in the active organization context. The project must belong to the selected organization, and requests for projects outside that organization must be rejected. This protects tenant isolation while still allowing project members and authorized managers to inspect project information.

If the project does not exist in the selected organization, the service must return a not-found response. If the caller lacks project visibility in the current organization, the service must reject the request with an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId and the currently selected organization scope in a single lookup. Verify that the caller has project:view permission in the active organization context before returning data.

Query erp_hrm_time_projects by primary identifier and organization boundary. Do not return a project from another organization even if the identifier matches. Map the entity fields directly from the table, including name, description, color code, status, budget hours, start date, and end date, along with any other actual project columns present in the schema.

Return 404 when the project is not found within the current organization. Return 403 when the caller lacks permission. The endpoint has no request body and must not perform pagination or filtering.

responseBody.description: The full project record for the requested project.

operations.description:
Update an existing project in the selected organization.

This operation allows project managers to edit the project’s name, description, color code, status, budget hours, and planning dates. It supports ongoing project maintenance so teams can keep project identity, schedule, and visual presentation current while work is in progress.

The project belongs to a single organization, so the update is always applied within the caller’s current organization context. The project color code is used for visual distinction in the user interface, and planning fields such as description, budget hours, start date, and end date are optional business details that help with planning and tracking.

The server must reject updates when the caller lacks project management permission, when the project does not exist in the current organization, or when the requested status change violates project lifecycle rules. The updated project is returned after persistence so clients can refresh any project lists, details, or dashboards that depend on the changed data.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the current organization context. Verify the caller has project management permission.

Apply only mutable fields from the request body to the project record. Validate required fields such as name and color code when they are present in the update payload, and preserve existing values for omitted optional fields according to the update DTO semantics.

Enforce organization isolation so the project must belong to the caller’s selected organization. Reject the request with not found if the project does not exist in that organization.

Validate lifecycle status transitions against the project business rules. Allow updates to active, archived, or completed only when the transition is permitted by the project workflow. Do not allow any change that would conflict with the rule that archived and completed projects remain viewable but cannot receive new timelogs.

Persist the updated project in a transaction. Return the full updated project entity. If downstream invariants are enforced at the service layer, ensure any invalid combination of schedule, status, or display fields is rejected with a clear validation error.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a project from the current organization when deletion rules are satisfied.

This operation is intended for project management workflows where a project is no longer needed and has no recorded work history. A project can only be removed if it belongs to the active organization context and does not have any associated timelogs. This protects historical time data from being lost and ensures cross-tenant isolation is preserved.

The caller must have project management authority in the current organization. If the project still has timelogs, the request must be rejected. If the project does not exist in the current organization context, the request must fail as not found. Successful deletion removes the project record and any project-local associations that are deleted together by the persistence layer, while preserving unrelated organization data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the active organization context. Verify that the caller has project management permission in the current organization.

Before deleting, check for any timelog records referencing the project. If at least one timelog exists, reject the request with a conflict-style error and do not delete the project. If the project is missing in the current organization context, return not found.

Perform the delete in a transaction to avoid race conditions between the pre-check and deletion. Ensure the deletion respects organization isolation so a project from another organization cannot be removed even if the identifier is known. Return the deleted project representation if the service layer convention expects a body for successful destructive operations; otherwise return no content.

operations.description:
Retrieve the list of employees assigned to a project.

This operation returns the current project team composition for the specified project, including each employee's membership record and assignment role within that project. It is used to browse who participates in the project and to distinguish between general members and project leads.

The result is scoped to the selected project and therefore reflects only the memberships belonging to that project. It supports paginated browsing for project staffing screens and should be used together with project detail and membership management operations when viewing or maintaining the team structure.

If the project does not exist or the caller is not allowed to view project membership data, the request must be rejected. The response should remain consistent with the project's current memberships and should not include employees from other projects.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_project_memberships for the given erp_hrm_time_project_id.
Join the employee relation so the list can be presented as project team composition, but keep the primary response focused on membership records. Apply pagination and any supported search/sort filters in the request body according to list browsing conventions.

Enforce that the target project exists and belongs to the current organization context before querying. Reject access when the caller lacks project visibility or management rights. Preserve the unique project-employee constraint already enforced by the database; this operation is read-only and must not create or modify memberships.

Use the project_role field as the assignment role for each row. Include employee-linked summary data only if the corresponding summary DTO exists in the component model; otherwise, return the membership entity/summary shape that matches the generated schema. Handle empty results by returning an empty page rather than an error.

operations.description:
Create a project membership for an employee within the selected project.

This operation assigns one employee to one project and records the employee's role within that project team, such as a regular member or project lead. It is used for project staffing and for determining who is eligible to participate in project work and task management within the project scope.

The project membership is organization-scoped through the selected organization context. The project identified by `{projectId}` and the employee referenced in the request must both belong to the same organization, and the employee must not already be assigned to the project. If the project or employee cannot be resolved in the current organization, or if the membership already exists, the request must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target project by id within the current organization context and verify that it exists. Validate that the request employee belongs to the same organization and that the employee is eligible to be added to the project.

Check the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_project_id, erp_hrm_time_employee_id) before inserting. If a membership already exists for the employee and project pair, return a conflict-style validation error and do not create a duplicate row.

Persist a new erp_hrm_time_project_memberships row using the path projectId, the requested employee id, and the requested project_role. The service should create the record in a transaction so concurrent duplicate assignments cannot bypass the uniqueness rule. Return the created membership with its linked project and employee context if the API layer uses entity expansion.

If the organization context is missing, the project is not accessible, the employee does not belong to the same organization, or the provided role value is invalid, reject the request with a clear business error.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project membership for a specific project.

This operation returns the employee assignment record that connects one employee to one project and identifies the employee's role within that project team, such as member or project lead. It is useful for viewing the current composition of a project team and confirming who is assigned to participate in the project.

The membership is always resolved within the selected organization and the specified project. If the project or membership does not exist in the current organization, or if the membership does not belong to the specified project, the request must fail with an appropriate not-found response. Access must also respect the platform's project visibility and management permissions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the current organization context, then load the project membership by membershipId constrained to that same project. Verify that the membership belongs to the project and that the project itself belongs to the selected organization. Return the full project membership entity including its employee and assigned project role fields as defined by the schema.

Do not allow cross-organization access. If either the project or membership is missing, or if the membership is associated with a different project, respond with a 404-style not-found error. This endpoint is read-only and must not modify membership data. Authorization should allow users with project viewing capability and users with project management capability, according to the organization permission model.

Remove an employee from a project by deleting the project membership record.

This operation ends the association between one employee and one project inside the currently selected organization. It is intended for project staffing changes, team restructuring, and lead reassignment workflows. Because project memberships are independent, removing one membership does not affect the employee's assignments to other projects.

Only users with project management permission may perform this action. The membership must belong to the project identified in the path, and the project must be accessible in the current organization context. If the membership does not exist, does not belong to the specified project, or the caller lacks permission, the request is rejected. If the removed employee was marked as a project lead for that project, the project leadership capability for that specific project ends immediately.
operations.name: erase

Load the target project membership by membershipId, ensuring it belongs to projectId and to the current organization context.

Delete the membership record only; do not touch any other memberships for the same employee.
After deletion, the employee must no longer be considered assigned to that project, and any project-lead flag for that membership is implicitly revoked by removal.
Do not cascade-delete employee, project, task, or timelog records.
Return the deleted membership representation so the client can refresh local team state. Handle concurrent deletion safely by treating already-removed memberships as not found.

Retrieve a paginated list of tasks for a specific project.

This operation returns the tasks that belong to the selected project and supports browsing work items by status, priority, assignee, and due date. It is intended for users who need to review and manage task progress inside the current project context.

The task list is scoped by project and must only include records from that project. Filtering and pagination apply within the project boundary, and the response is optimized for list views rather than full task details. The task title, description, status, priority, estimated hours, and due date are core task fields that shape list browsing and planning behavior.

If the project does not exist, or the caller lacks permission to view tasks in the project, the service must return an appropriate authorization or not-found error. Invalid filter values, malformed pagination settings, or attempts to query outside the project scope should be rejected before executing the database query.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId and verify the caller has access to the project within the current organization context.
Use the task table as the primary source and filter rows by the project foreign key.
Apply optional filters from the request body for status, priority, and assigned employee; combine them with pagination and sorting rules from the list-search contract.
Return tasks ordered according to the requested sort fields when provided, otherwise apply a stable default order suitable for task browsing.
Join only what is necessary for summary output, avoiding expensive detail joins unless required by the summary DTO.
Ensure assignee filters respect project scope and do not return tasks assigned to employees outside the selected organization.
Reject invalid enum values, negative pagination values, or unsupported sort fields with a validation error.
If the project is missing, return not found. If the user cannot view the project or tasks within it, return forbidden.
Use the paginated response wrapper for task summaries.

operations.description:
Create a new task within a project.

This operation creates a project work item inside the selected project context. A task belongs to exactly one project, starts in the open status by default, and may include a description, priority, estimated hours, due date, an assigned employee, and a parent task for one-level subtask nesting.

The assigned employee, when provided, must be a member of the same project. The parent task, when provided, must also belong to the same project. Only users with project management permission or project-lead authority for this project can create tasks here.

If the project is not eligible for task creation, or if the assigned employee or parent task does not match the project scope, the request must be rejected with a validation error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target project by id within the current organization context and verify that it exists and is not deleted. Enforce authorization so only users with project:manage permission or a project-lead membership for the same project can create tasks.

Validate the request body against the task creation rules: title is required; description, estimated_hours, due_date, assigned employee, and parent task are optional; priority must be one of the supported task priorities; the new task status must be set to open regardless of client input. If an assigned employee id is provided, confirm that the employee is assigned to the same project through erp_hrm_time_project_memberships. If a parent task id is provided, confirm that it belongs to the same project and that the nesting depth does not exceed one level.

Persist the task in erp_hrm_time_tasks with the project foreign key, optional employee and parent_task references, and audit timestamps. Do not create history entries here unless the implementation layer explicitly records status creation events elsewhere. Return the created task entity. Reject requests for missing project, invalid scope, unauthorized access, invalid assignment, or invalid parent task with the appropriate domain error.

responseBody.description: The newly created task, including its project context and current state.

Retrieve a single task within a project.

This operation returns the full task record for the specified project and task identifiers, including the task title, description, current status, priority, estimated effort, due date, and assigned employee reference. Tasks are always scoped to a project, so the project path parameter is required to resolve the task in the correct project context.

The task entity also supports a one-level parent task relationship for subtasks. Consumers can use this endpoint to inspect a task’s current state and its assignment within the project. Access must respect the caller’s organization context and project visibility rules, and the task must belong to the given project.

If the task does not exist, does not belong to the specified project, or is not accessible in the current organization context, the request should fail with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at

Load the task by project scope first, then resolve the task by its id within the same organization. Verify that the task belongs to the given project before returning it.

Use a join or relation load against erp_hrm_time_projects and erp_hrm_time_tasks to ensure the path projectId and taskId refer to the same organization-scoped project/task pair. Return the full task record fields defined in erp_hrm_time_tasks: id, erp_hrm_time_project_id, erp_hrm_time_employee_id, parent_task_id, title, description, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

Do not include child task collections in the response. If the task is not found under the specified project, return 404. If the caller lacks access to the organization or project, return the standard authorization error.

operations.description:
Update a task that belongs to a specific project.

This endpoint lets authorized users edit task details within the context of a single project. A task may include a title, description, status, priority, estimated hours, due date, assigned employee, and parent task. The task remains scoped to the project identified in the path, and any assigned employee must be a member of that same project.

Task status changes are tracked as part of the task history, so consumers should expect the system to record status transitions when the status value changes. The endpoint also preserves the one-level subtask structure by allowing a parent task only within the same project.

Authorization is limited to users who can manage the project or act as a project lead for that project. Validation errors are returned when the task does not exist, the project context does not match, the assigned employee is not part of the project, the parent task is invalid, or the caller lacks sufficient permission.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the task by projectId and taskId in the same query scope to ensure the task belongs to the specified project. Verify organization context from the authenticated member before any modification.

Authorize if the caller has project:manage permission or is a project lead for the target project. Reject access if neither condition is met.

Validate update payload fields against task business rules: title is required for persisted state, status must be one of the allowed task states, priority must be one of the allowed values, estimated hours and due date are optional, and description may be null or empty depending on DTO definition. If assigned employee is provided, confirm the employee belongs to the same project. If parent task is provided, confirm it exists, belongs to the same project, and does not create deeper nesting beyond one level.

If status changes, write a task history entry capturing the previous status, new status, timestamp, and acting user. Use a transaction so the task update and history insert succeed or fail together.

Return not found when the task does not exist within the specified project. Return validation errors for invalid assignee/parent relationships. Return forbidden for insufficient permissions. Preserve all other fields not included in the update request.

Permanently removes a task from a project.

This operation is used to delete a project task within the current organization context. The task must belong to the project identified by `projectId`, and the caller must have permission to manage tasks in that project. Tasks may be part of a project hierarchy and may have history entries, so the service must validate project ownership before deletion and reject attempts to delete a task that does not belong to the specified project.

Deletion is intended for project-managed work items and affects only the targeted task record. Related behavior such as task history visibility, subtasks, and any downstream business rules must be enforced by the service layer according to project and task constraints. If the task cannot be deleted because it is protected by domain rules or the identifiers do not match, the request must fail with an appropriate error.
operations.name: erase

Load the project by projectId within the current organization context and verify that the caller is authorized to manage tasks for that project. Then load the task by taskId and confirm it belongs to the specified project. If the task does not exist, return not found. If the task exists but belongs to a different project or organization, return not found or forbidden according to the service's access policy.

Delete the task record using a transaction-safe operation. If the database enforces foreign key constraints from child subtasks or history records, the implementation must rely on the existing domain rules for task deletion and surface a business error when deletion is not allowed. Do not accept a request body. Return success with no content on completion.

operations.description:
Retrieve the status-change history for a specific task within a project.

This operation returns the immutable audit trail of task status transitions, including the time of each change, the previous status, the new status, and the member who made the update. It is intended for project members, project leads, and users with project management privileges who need to review how a task evolved over time.

The history is scoped to the selected organization, the specified project, and the specified task. If the caller cannot access the parent project or the task does not belong to the provided project, the request is rejected. Because history entries are part of the audit record, this endpoint is read-only and only supports browsing through paginated results.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load task history entries for the given project and task, ensuring the task belongs to the provided project and both belong to the current organization context. Use the task history entries table as an immutable source of status transition records. Apply pagination, sorting by recorded timestamp descending by default, and return a paginated summary payload.

Do not allow modification of history data. If the task is not found in the current organization or does not belong to the provided project, return a not-found or forbidden-style error according to the service convention. If the caller lacks permission to view tasks in the project, reject the request. The response must include only fields needed for list rendering, such as timestamp, previous status, new status, and actor reference, while preserving the audit trail integrity.

responseBody.description: Paginated task history entries for the requested task.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single task history entry for a task within a project.

This operation returns the immutable audit record that was created when a task status changed. The record is scoped to the specified project and task, so consumers can inspect the exact change history for a task without mixing entries from other tasks, projects, or organizations.

The returned history entry preserves the original timestamp, the previous status, the new status, and the user who made the change. Because task history is part of the audit trail, this endpoint is read-only and is intended for task detail screens, project activity views, and administrative review workflows.

The request is authorized within the currently selected organization context. If the project, task, or history entry does not exist in that scope, or if the caller is not allowed to view the project task data, the service must respond with an appropriate not-found or forbidden error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the current organization from the authenticated member context, then verify that the project belongs to that organization and that the task belongs to the specified project. After that, load the history entry by its identifier while enforcing that it belongs to the specified task.

Use a single read query with joins or equivalent repository checks to ensure the project-task-history hierarchy is consistent before returning data. Do not allow history entries to be fetched across projects or organizations. The entry is immutable, so no update logic applies.

Return 404 when the project, task, or history entry is missing or not linked through the specified hierarchy. Return 403 when the caller lacks permission to view the task/project scope. The response should include the full history entry entity as defined by the task history schema, including the stored status transition metadata and actor information. Keep the endpoint read-only and do not expose any mutation behavior.

responseBody.description: The full task history entry for the specified project task.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of timelogs for the current organization context.

This operation supports browsing daily work entries that record the date, duration, project, optional task, optional description, and billable status of each time entry. Timelogs are organization-scoped and are always filtered to the caller's selected organization. Depending on permissions, the response may include only the caller's own timelogs or all employees' timelogs in the organization.

The list supports filtering by date range, project, task, and billable status, along with pagination and sorting for efficient review. Use this endpoint to power employee time-entry screens, manager review pages, and organization-wide timelog searches.

Access is subject to permission checks and data visibility rules. Locked timelogs that belong to approved timesheets remain visible but are not editable through update or delete operations. Archived or completed projects may still appear in historical results, but they do not accept new entries.

Return validation errors when the search criteria are malformed, the organization context is missing, or the caller lacks the required visibility permission.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_timelogs within the active organization context only. Enforce member ownership restrictions unless the caller has time:view_all permission, in which case include all employees' timelogs for the organization. Support pagination, search filters, and sorting in the request body. Expected filters: date range, project, task, and billable flag. Joins may be required to resolve project/task scoping and to ensure returned rows belong to the active organization. Exclude data from other organizations at the query level.

Return a paginated summary projection ordered by the requested sort criteria, with sensible defaults such as most recent date first and stable tie-breaking by primary key. Validate that task filters belong to the selected project when both are supplied. Validate all referenced identifiers exist within the caller's organization. If the caller is not permitted to view other employees' timelogs, constrain the query to the authenticated employee only. Reject invalid page, size, and sorting parameters with standard validation errors.

responseBody.description: Paginated timelog summaries for the current organization context.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination, and sorting options for timelog browsing.

operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry for the current organization and employee.

This operation records a single day-based work entry with the selected project, optional task, logged duration, optional description, and billable flag. Timelogs are the base unit of time tracking and are used later in weekly timesheets, reporting, and timer conversion workflows.

The created timelog is always scoped to the authenticated employee in the current organization context. The service must validate that the selected project belongs to the same organization, that any provided task belongs to that project, and that the employee is allowed to create time entries. Existing locked or approved timesheet rules must be enforced so protected records cannot be altered through this endpoint.

If the target project is archived or completed, the request must be rejected. The operation should also ensure the employee is active, the work date is valid, and the duration is a positive value in minutes. On success, return the created timelog with its persisted identifiers and timestamps.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new row into erp_hrm_time_timelogs using the authenticated member as erp_hrm_time_member_id and the current organization-scoped employee as the owner context.
Validate that the employee belongs to the active organization and is active, that the project belongs to the same organization and is not archived or completed, and that any task belongs to the same project.
Use the provided work date, duration minutes, description, and billable flag; do not accept ownership overrides from the request body.
If the timelog is created from a running timer workflow, the timer conversion should be handled elsewhere; this endpoint only creates a manual timelog.
Emit any required activity log entry according to business rules after successful insert. Return the created entity with timestamps. Reject with a validation or conflict error when organization scope, project/task integrity, or employee status rules are violated.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog record.

requestBody.description: Timelog creation details for the current employee in the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog entry by its identifier.

This operation returns the full timelog record, including the employee who created it, the project it belongs to, the optional task association, the work date, duration, billable flag, description, and audit timestamps. It is intended for viewing a specific time entry in detail after selecting the current organization context.

Access to the record is limited by organization scope and by the caller's permissions. Ordinary employees can retrieve their own timelogs, while users with broader time-tracking visibility can retrieve timelogs across the selected organization. If the timelog does not exist in the current organization, or the caller is not allowed to view it, the request must fail with an appropriate not-found or forbidden response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timelog by primary key and eagerly validate organization scope through its related member, project, and optional task associations. Ensure the resolved timelog belongs to the caller's selected organization before returning it.

Return the full entity with its direct fields. Do not expose timelogs from other organizations. If the record is missing, or the caller lacks permission to view it, return an authorization-appropriate error. Preserve deleted records according to existing service policy only if they are still intended to be retrievable; otherwise treat deleted_at as hidden from normal reads.

No complex filtering or pagination is needed. This is a single-entity lookup, so use a straightforward read-by-id query with relation checks and consistent error handling.

responseBody.description: The full timelog record for the requested entry.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timelog to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog entry.

This operation allows an employee or an authorized manager to modify a single time entry within the currently selected organization. A timelog records the work date, logged duration in minutes, optional description, billable flag, and the project and optional task associated with the work.

The server must validate that the timelog belongs to the current organization context, that the referenced project and task remain valid, and that the task belongs to the selected project when present. If the timelog is included in an approved timesheet, it cannot be edited. If the timelog belongs to a draft or unsubmitted timesheet, edits are allowed only when the business rules permit it.

When validation fails, return an appropriate error for invalid identifiers, unauthorized access, or business-rule violations such as editing a locked timelog or assigning a task that does not belong to the project.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the timelog by id and ensure it belongs to the active organization through its member/project relationships. Reject the request if the timelog is not found in the current scope.

Before applying updates, verify that the timelog is not locked by an approved timesheet inclusion. If locked, reject with a business-rule error. Validate project membership and task consistency: the project must exist in the active organization, and when a task id is provided it must belong to the same project. If the project changes, ensure the existing or new task remains valid for that project.

Persist only editable fields from the request body: work_date, duration_minutes, description, billable, erp_hrm_time_project_id, and erp_hrm_time_task_id. Update updated_at on success. Do not allow changing ownership to another member through this endpoint. Return the updated timelog entity after save.

responseBody.description: The updated timelog record after successful validation and persistence.

parameters.description: Timelog identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Fields that can be changed on an existing timelog entry.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a timelog that belongs to the current organization and timelog context.

This operation supports employee self-service deletion for the owner of the time entry, as well as privileged deletion by users who have time management permission. The system checks the selected organization context before performing the deletion and ensures the target timelog is visible within that tenant boundary.

A timelog can only be deleted when it is not part of any submitted or approved timesheet. If the entry has already been included in a submitted timesheet, or locked by an approved timesheet, the request is rejected. When deletion is allowed, the timelog record is removed permanently and any related timesheet composition must remain consistent.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target timelog by ID within the authenticated member's selected organization context. Verify that the timelog exists and belongs to the same organization as the requester through its employee/project ownership chain as enforced by the service layer.

Authorize deletion using the following rules: allow if the requester has time management permission; otherwise allow only when the requester is the timelog owner. Reject with forbidden if neither condition is met.

Before deleting, check the timesheet link table for any association with submitted or approved timesheets. If any linked timesheet has status submitted or approved, reject the delete request with a business rule error because the timelog is locked by workflow state. If the timelog is not linked to any submitted or approved timesheet, delete the timelog row and any dependent composition rows that reference it, but do not alter historical timesheet records beyond maintaining referential integrity.

Return no content on success. If the timelog does not exist in the current organization, return not found. If the timelog is locked, return a conflict-style validation error. Ensure all checks are performed inside a transaction to avoid race conditions between timesheet approval and timelog deletion.

parameters.description: The identifier of the timelog to permanently delete within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Update the currently running timer for the authenticated employee.

This operation lets an employee adjust the live work session while it is still active. The editable context includes the selected project, an optional task, and the timer description so the running record can stay aligned with the actual work being performed.

The timer remains active after the update. If the timer has already been stopped or discarded, or if the requested project or task is not valid for the employee’s current organization context, the request is rejected. The response returns the updated timer state for use in live tracking interfaces.
operations.name: patch
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated employee and current organization context first. Find the employee's active timer; if none exists, return a not-found or conflict-style validation error depending on service conventions. Ensure the timer belongs to the current organization through its employee context.

Apply only the fields provided in the update request: project, task, and description. Validate that the selected project is assignable for the employee and that the selected task, when provided, belongs to that same project and is allowed by the project/task rules. Reject changes that would break the running timer invariants or violate one-active-timer-per-employee behavior.

Persist the timer update without changing its running status. Do not create a timelog here; timelog creation belongs to the stop flow. If the timer is already stopped or discarded, return an error indicating the timer is no longer editable. Return the current timer entity after persistence so the UI can keep displaying the live session state.

responseBody.description: The updated running timer after its context has been changed.

requestBody.description: Editable context for the active running timer.

operations.description:
Start a new running timer for the current employee.

This operation begins a live work session within the selected organization context and stores the timer context, including the chosen project, optional task, and optional description. The timer remains active until the employee stops or discards it, and it is used as the source for later timelog creation when the session ends.

The timer is tied to the current employee and must respect organization boundaries. The selected project must belong to the same organization, and any task provided must belong to that project. If the employee already has an active timer, the request is rejected. If the employee is deactivated or otherwise not allowed to track time, the request is also rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticate the member and resolve the current organization context before any database write.
Create a new erp_hrm_time_timers row for the current employee only if there is no existing active timer for that employee. Validate that the referenced project belongs to the selected organization and is eligible for time tracking. If taskId is provided, validate that the task exists, belongs to the same project, and is accessible in the current organization.

Persist the timer start timestamp using the server clock. Store the optional description as provided. If the schema contains only the timer context fields, write only those fields and leave all database-managed fields untouched. Return a conflict-style error when a timer is already active, and a not-found or validation error when the project/task context is invalid.

Do not create a timelog here; timelog creation happens when the timer is stopped. Ensure all queries are constrained by the selected organization and employee identity so timers cannot be created across tenants or on behalf of another employee.

responseBody.description: The newly created running timer with its active context.

requestBody.description: Timer start context for the current employee, including the project and optional task to track work against.

prerequisites.description: A running timer requires a valid project to exist first, because the timer request must reference an existing project_id within the current organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve the currently running timer for a specific employee timer record.

This endpoint returns the live timer session context, including the selected project, optional task, start timestamp, and any description captured while the timer is running. It is intended for the employee's active timer view so the client can display the current work session and allow the user to continue, edit, stop, or discard it.

The timer belongs to the current organization context and is tied to a member account, an employee record, a project, and optionally a task. Consumers should expect the full timer record and use the related identifiers to resolve project and task details in the UI. If the timer does not exist or is not accessible in the current organization scope, the request must fail with a not-found or forbidden response as appropriate.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timer by its UUID primary key and verify it belongs to the current authenticated member and selected organization context through the linked employee. Join or hydrate the related member, employee, project, and optional task references as needed for the full entity response.

Do not return timers that have been discarded or belong to another organization. Since the table has a unique constraint on employee_id, the service may also use this endpoint to confirm the single running timer for the employee when the caller is authorized. Preserve deleted_at in the payload only if the underlying entity contract exposes it, but do not infer additional lifecycle behavior beyond the schema and timer rules.

Handle missing timer, cross-organization access, and deleted/discarded records as not found. The operation is read-only and must not mutate the timer state.

responseBody.description: The full running timer record, including its project and optional task context.

parameters.description: The timer identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Update a running timer's work context.

This operation allows an employee to correct the project, optional task, or description of an active timer while the live session is still running. The timer remains active after the update, and the edited context is used when the timer is later stopped to create the resulting timelog.

The timer belongs to the currently selected organization context and is tied to a single employee. Validation must ensure the timer is still running, the selected project is available to the employee, and any task belongs to that project and is valid for the employee's work context. Requests that attempt to modify a stopped or discarded timer, or that violate project/task assignment rules, must be rejected with a validation error.

This endpoint is closely related to the timer start, stop, and discard operations. Successful updates should preserve the timer's active state and only change the editable fields allowed by the running timer workflow.
operations.name: putByTimerid
operations.specification:
Load the timer by timerId within the authenticated member's selected organization. Confirm the timer belongs to the current employee context and is still running; reject updates for stopped or discarded timers.

Apply only mutable running-timer fields from the request body. Validate that the project exists in the same organization and that the employee is allowed to track time against it. If a task is provided, verify that it belongs to the selected project and that the task is compatible with the employee's project membership rules.

Update the timer atomically without changing its running state. Do not create a timelog here; timelog creation happens only when the timer is stopped. If the timer record cannot be found, return not found. If the project/task combination is invalid or the timer is no longer active, return a domain validation error.

responseBody.description: The updated running timer after its work context has been changed.

parameters.description: Identifier of the running timer to update within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timerId

requestBody.description: Fields used to update the running timer's project, optional task, and description while it is active.

operations.description:
Discard a running timer for the current organization context.

This operation removes a timer entry that is being used for live time tracking. It is intended for employees who want to abandon an active work session without creating a timelog, and for administrators or time managers who need to clean up timer records within their organization scope.

The timer is always evaluated within the selected organization and the caller's permissions. A normal employee may discard only their own timer, while users with time management permission may remove timers for any employee in the same organization. If the timer cannot be found, does not belong to the current organization, or the caller is not allowed to remove it, the request fails.

This operation is related to timelog creation because stopping a timer creates a timelog, while discarding it does not. After deletion, the timer is no longer available for editing, stopping, or resuming.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the timer by timerId within the current organization context. Verify the timer exists and belongs to the organization selected for the request. Enforce authorization so that the owning employee may delete only their own active timer, while users with time management permission may delete any timer in the same organization.

If the timer is already discarded or otherwise not deletable according to the timer lifecycle, return a not-found or conflict-style error consistent with the service conventions. When deletion succeeds, remove the timer row from the database in a transaction-safe way; no timelog should be created for this endpoint. Do not touch timelogs, timesheets, or other linked records.

Return the deleted timer entity so the client can update live timer UI state. Ensure cross-organization access is blocked even if the identifier is guessed. Log the action if the system records activity for timer discard events.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timer to discard within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of timesheets for the currently selected organization.

Employees can use this endpoint to find their own timesheets by week or status, while users with approval permission can browse submitted timesheets across the organization. Results are always limited to the active organization context and never include timesheets from other organizations.

Filtering supports timesheet status and week/date range criteria, and the list is paginated for efficient browsing. The returned summary data is intended for list views and should reflect the current organization scope, including access restrictions for draft, submitted, approved, and rejected timesheets.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_timesheets for the currently selected organization only.
Apply organization scoping from the authenticated member's active organization context before any other filter.
Support pagination, sorting, and filtering by status and week/date range through the request body.
For employees without approval permission, restrict results to their own timesheets only; for users with time approval permission, allow access to all timesheets in the organization as permitted by business rules.
Do not return records from any other organization.
Use the timesheet owner and status rules to ensure draft/rejected self-service behavior remains consistent with the domain rules.
Return a paginated summary payload suitable for list rendering, including fields needed to display week boundaries, status, total hours, and review/submission state if present.
If the request contains invalid date ranges, unsupported filters, or pagination values, return a validation error. If the active organization context is missing, return an authorization/context error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries scoped to the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for browsing organization-scoped timesheets.

operations.description:
Create a new weekly timesheet draft for the current employee.

This operation starts the timesheet workflow for a specific Monday-to-Sunday week and returns the newly created draft timesheet so the employee can review, adjust included timelogs, and submit it later. The timesheet belongs to the currently selected organization and is always created for the authenticated member's own employee record.

The created timesheet is used in the approval flow for time tracking. When a draft is created, the system may include eligible timelogs for that employee within the requested week, and the resulting record must remain within the same organization context. Requests that target another organization, another employee, or an invalid week must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a timesheet draft for the authenticated member's employee in the selected organization.
Validate that the request is scoped to the current organization context and that the user has an employee record in that organization.
Validate the requested week boundaries from the request body and ensure they represent the intended weekly timesheet period.
Prevent creation if a conflicting timesheet for the same employee and week already exists in a non-allowed state according to the timesheet workflow.
Persist the new timesheet and associate any eligible timelogs for that employee and week according to the service rules.
Recompute total hours from the included timelogs so the stored total matches the current contents.
Return the created timesheet entity with its linked timelogs and status information.
If the employee is deactivated or otherwise blocked from time entry, reject the request with a business validation error.
If organization context is missing or the employee does not belong to the selected organization, reject with an authorization or scope error.

responseBody.description: The created weekly timesheet draft, including its current status and calculated totals.

requestBody.description: Data required to create a weekly timesheet draft for the current employee.

operations.description:
Retrieve a weekly timesheet and its review metadata.

This operation returns one timesheet record for the currently selected organization, including the employee owner, week boundaries, submission state, review timestamps, rejection reason, and the reviewer when one has been assigned. The timesheet belongs to exactly one employee and represents that employee's weekly time record, so the returned data must always remain scoped to the organization and the owning employee relationship stored in the database.

Employees may use this endpoint to open their own timesheets, while users with timesheet approval permission may use it to inspect submitted timesheets during review. The associated timelogs are represented through the timesheet-to-timelog relationship and must be loaded consistently with the timesheet so the consumer sees the complete weekly composition. If the record belongs to another organization, does not exist, or is not visible to the current actor under organization-scoped access rules, the service must reject the request with an access or not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timesheet by id, then join its owner employee, optional reviewer member, and associated timesheet-timelog links with their timelog records.

Before returning data, enforce selected-organization isolation by verifying that the resolved employee belongs to the current organization context. Deny access if the timesheet does not belong to the selected organization or if the caller lacks permission to view it. Employees may view their own timesheets; approvers with time approval permission may view submitted timesheets in the organization. Do not expose any record from a different organization.

Return the full entity shape expected for a detail view, including relationship-derived data needed by the consumer. Preserve database values for status, submitted_at, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, and timestamps exactly as stored. If the record is absent or hidden by authorization rules, return a not-found or forbidden response according to the service's standard error policy.

responseBody.description: A full timesheet record with owner, review metadata, and associated weekly composition.

parameters.description: Timesheet identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Update a weekly timesheet for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint lets the owning employee adjust a draft or rejected timesheet by adding or removing included timelogs, while also supporting authorized review actions on submitted timesheets. A timesheet always belongs to exactly one employee, and all access is limited to the active organization context.

The total hours on the timesheet are derived from the timelogs included in that weekly record. When the included timelogs change, the stored total must be kept in sync with the current contents. Submitted timesheets can be reviewed only by users with approval permission, and rejection requires a reason to be recorded with the review action.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by timesheetId within the current organization context. Verify that the timesheet exists and belongs to the selected organization before any update is applied.

Enforce business rules by actor and status:
- The owning employee may update only their own timesheet when it is in draft or rejected status.
- Users with time:approve permission may review submitted timesheets.
- Prevent modifications when the timesheet belongs to another employee, when the status is not editable for the requester, or when the timesheet is in a state that does not allow the requested change.

When the request changes the set of included timelogs, validate that every referenced timelog belongs to the same organization and to the same owning employee, and that the timelogs are allowed to be part of the week being edited. Recompute total hours from the included timelogs so the stored value matches the current composition.

If the request performs an approval, set status to approved, store the reviewer identity and review timestamp, and preserve the approved set of timelogs. If the request performs a rejection, require a rejection reason, set status to rejected, and store the reviewer identity and review timestamp. If the request is a self-service edit on a draft or rejected timesheet, update the included timelogs and derived total hours only.

Reject updates that try to cross organization boundaries, alter another employee’s timesheet, submit fields that are not permitted for the requester’s role, or attempt to modify a timesheet in a non-editable state. Return validation or authorization errors as appropriate.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet record after the modification is applied.

parameters.description: The identifier of the timesheet to update.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Timesheet update data, including allowed timelog adjustments or review fields depending on the caller's permission and the current timesheet status.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a weekly timesheet for the current organization context.

A timesheet represents an employee’s collected timelogs for a specific week, along with its submission and review state. This operation removes the timesheet record when the caller is allowed to do so and when the timesheet is in a deletable state. The service must respect ownership and permission rules so that only authorized users can delete the record.

Deletion must be rejected when the timesheet is already submitted or approved, because those states lock the included timelogs and preserve review history. The service must also reject requests for timesheets that do not belong to the current organization context or that the caller is not permitted to access. If the deletion succeeds, the response can return the removed timesheet for confirmation and UI refresh.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by timesheetId within the authenticated organization context.
Verify the caller is authorized: the owner may delete their own draft timesheet, and permission-based staff may delete according to the organization rules. Reject access when the timesheet is outside the current organization or not visible to the caller.

Before deletion, enforce lifecycle constraints from the requirements: timesheets in submitted or approved status must not be deleted. If the schema has a relationship table linking timesheets and timelogs, delete the association rows first or within the same transaction, then delete the timesheet row itself. Do not delete timelogs unless the schema or business rules explicitly require it; the system only removes the timesheet record and its composition links.

Use a transaction so that relationship cleanup and parent deletion succeed or fail together. Return a not-found error when the timesheetId does not exist in scope, and a conflict or validation error when the status prevents deletion. Record an activity log entry only if the broader system uses activity logging for destructive timesheet actions and the schema supports it.

parameters.description: The identifier of the timesheet to delete, scoped to the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Update the timelogs included in a weekly timesheet.

This operation lets the owning employee manage the timelog set for a draft or rejected timesheet, and it allows permitted organization users to adjust timesheet contents according to their role and organization context. The timesheet remains scoped to a single organization and a single employee, and the final total hours are derived from the timelogs currently linked to it.

The system enforces that only timelogs belonging to the same organization, employee, and target week can be included. Timelogs that are part of an approved timesheet remain locked and cannot be edited through this composition workflow. If the timesheet is not in a mutable state, the request must be rejected. If the resulting timesheet would have no timelogs, or if the selected timelogs violate ownership, organization, or approval-state rules, the operation must fail with a validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id within the current organization context. Verify that the authenticated member is allowed to modify this timesheet: either the employee owner editing their own draft or rejected timesheet, or a user with the appropriate approval/manage permissions when the business workflow allows it. Reject access across organization boundaries.

Read the requested timelog membership changes from the request body and resolve the timelog ids to actual timelog rows. Ensure every timelog belongs to the same organization and, for self-service flows, to the timesheet owner. Prevent inclusion of timelogs that are locked because they are part of an approved timesheet. Prevent duplicates and ignore or reject ids that do not exist, belong to another employee, or fall outside the timesheet week.

Apply the membership changes atomically using the join table for timesheet timelogs. After the link set is updated, recalculate total hours from the linked timelogs so the timesheet summary remains consistent. Preserve approved timesheets as immutable; if the timesheet is approved, reject any change. If the timesheet is submitted and the workflow does not allow edits, reject the request.

Return the refreshed timesheet entity or updated summary so clients can display the new total hours and current status immediately. Surface validation errors for invalid state, inaccessible resources, cross-organization references, locked timelogs, and attempts to edit another employee’s timesheet.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet with recalculated totals and current status after timelog membership changes.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet to update within the current organization.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Timelog membership changes to apply to the timesheet.

operations.description:
Add a timelog to a draft timesheet for the owning employee.

This operation updates the weekly timesheet composition by associating an existing timelog with the selected timesheet. It is intended for employee-owned timesheets and must respect the ownership and week boundaries of the parent record. The resulting timesheet reflects the updated set of included timelogs and the derived total hours for that week.

The operation is only valid when the target timesheet belongs to the current employee, is in a modifiable state, and the timelog being attached belongs to the same employee and week context. Timelogs that are already included, locked by approval, or otherwise incompatible with the timesheet state must be rejected with a validation error. If the timesheet is rejected, it may be modified again while in draft status after rejection, but approved timesheets remain locked.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the parent timesheet by timesheetId within the current organization context and current authenticated employee scope. Verify the timesheet exists, belongs to the caller, and is not approved. Then validate that the requested timelog exists, belongs to the same employee, is in the same organization, and is not already linked to the target timesheet.

Insert the link in erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs only after checking that the timelog is allowed to be included in the timesheet state. Recompute the timesheet's derived total hours from the included timelogs after the association is created. If the persistence model stores the total as a derived value, update it in the same transaction so the list/detail views remain consistent.

Reject the request when the timelog is already included, when the timesheet is not owned by the current employee, when the timesheet is approved, when the timelog is locked by an approved timesheet, or when the timelog does not belong to the same employee/week context required by the business rules. Use a transaction to prevent duplicate links and race conditions. Return the updated timesheet representation or the updated parent composition view as defined by the response schema.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet after the timelog has been added, including the recalculated composition and total hours.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet that will receive the timelog, scoped to the current employee's weekly record.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Identifies the timelog to add to the selected timesheet.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog entry associated with a specific weekly timesheet.

This operation returns the relationship record that links one timesheet to one timelog, allowing clients to inspect which work logs are included in a given weekly submission. The association belongs to exactly one employee-owned timesheet and exactly one timelog, and it is used to support weekly composition, review, and approval workflows.

Access is constrained by organization context and ownership rules. Employees may read their own timesheet contents, while users with approval permission may read submitted timesheet contents for review. The implementation must verify that the requested association belongs to the specified timesheet, that the timesheet exists in the current organization scope, and that the caller is authorized to view it. If either identifier does not match the stored relationship, the request must be rejected as not found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timesheet_timelogs row by id and ensure it belongs to the parent timesheet id from the route. Join the related timesheet and timelog records only as needed to validate organization scope and caller access.

Authorization rules:
- Allow the owning employee to read their own timesheet association.
- Allow a user with timesheet approval permission to read associations for submitted timesheets they can review.
- Deny access across organization boundaries.

Validation rules:
- Return 404 if the association id does not exist or does not belong to the provided timesheet id.
- Return 404 if the parent timesheet does not exist in the current organization scope.
- Do not expose unrelated timelog data beyond the association entity unless the response schema requires it.

Implementation notes:
- Use the join table as the primary source of truth for the relationship.
- Preserve referential integrity expectations from the schema, including cascade-linked parents.
- If the association row is soft deleted, treat it as not found unless the service layer has an explicit recovery path, which this endpoint does not expose.

responseBody.description: The timelog-to-timesheet association that belongs to the requested weekly timesheet.

parameters.description: Identifier of the parent timesheet in the current organization scope.
parameters.name: timesheetId

parameters.description: Identifier of the timelog association within the parent timesheet.
parameters.name: timesheetTimelogId

operations.description:
Remove a timelog from a specific timesheet.

This operation lets an employee adjust the contents of a weekly timesheet by removing one included timelog from the selected timesheet. It is intended for timesheet editing workflows where draft or rejected submissions may be revised before being submitted again.

The operation only affects the relationship between the timesheet and the timelog. It does not delete the timelog record itself, and it does not modify the underlying time entry data. The timesheet and timelog must both belong to the currently selected organization context, and the timelog must actually be included in the specified timesheet.

The system should reject the request when the timesheet is already approved or otherwise locked, when the timelog is not associated with the timesheet, or when the caller does not have permission to modify the timesheet. If the relationship is removed successfully, the timesheet remains available for further edits and its totals should be recalculated from the remaining included timelogs.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the timesheet by timesheetId within the current organization context and verify that the caller is allowed to modify it. Allow the operation only when the timesheet is in an editable state, such as draft or rejected, and deny removal when the timesheet is approved or otherwise locked.

Verify that the timelog relationship identified by timesheetTimelogId exists in erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs for the given timesheet. If the link does not exist, return a not-found error. Do not delete the timelog record from erp_hrm_time_timelogs; delete only the join row that associates the timelog to the timesheet.

After deleting the join record, recompute any derived timesheet totals or cached summaries that depend on the included timelog set. If the timesheet becomes empty, keep the timesheet record unless another business rule explicitly removes it; this operation only removes one included timelog.

Return a conflict or forbidden error when the timesheet is locked, approved, or otherwise not editable. Return not found when either the timesheet or the specific association is not visible in the current organization context. Ensure all checks are scoped to the caller's organization and employee ownership or approval permissions.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet that currently includes the timelog.
parameters.name: timesheetId

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet-to-timelog association to remove within the specified timesheet.
parameters.name: timesheetTimelogId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated set of time report rows for the selected organization.

This report supports operational review of logged time across employees, projects, and tasks. It is intended for users who can view organization reports and need to analyze totals by date range, grouping mode, and other report filters. The returned rows preserve the distinction between billable and non-billable time so reporting remains accurate for review and budgeting purposes.

The endpoint only returns data within the currently selected organization and must reject requests from users who do not have report access. Results should reflect the report criteria exactly, including grouping, date boundaries, and any employee, project, or billable filters. If no rows match the requested criteria, the response should be an empty page rather than an error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the organization-scoped time report row source for the selected organization only.
Apply request filters for date range, employee, project, billable status, and grouping mode as defined by the report request DTO.
Return paginated report rows sorted consistently for stable UI browsing.
Enforce report:view authorization before executing the query and reject access when the caller lacks permission in the selected organization.
Preserve billable/non-billable distinctions in all aggregates and summaries.
If the filter combination yields no matching data, return an empty page.
Validate all date-range inputs and reject malformed or inverted ranges.
Do not expose rows from other organizations under any circumstance.

responseBody.description: Paginated time report rows for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Time report search criteria including grouping, date range, pagination, and report filters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a precomputed time report row for the selected organization.

This operation returns one aggregated reporting slice from the organization time-report dataset. Each row represents logged time summarized by reporting date and, when applicable, by employee, project, task, and billable status.

The result is scoped to the currently selected organization and is intended for report consumers who need to inspect a single reporting row in detail. Because the source table is maintained by reporting jobs, this endpoint is read-only and does not create or modify report data. If the requested row does not belong to the selected organization, the row is not found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the report row by its UUID primary key and ensure the record belongs to the caller's selected organization context. Use a single indexed lookup on the primary key, then verify the organization scope before returning the row. Do not expose rows from other organizations.

Return the full entity mapped from erp_hrm_time_time_report_rows, including optional employee, project, and task references, along with report_date, billable, logged_minutes, logged_hours, created_at, and updated_at. The deleted_at field exists on the table but should not be treated as user-editable data. If row access is disallowed by organization scope or the record does not exist, return not found. No request body is required.

responseBody.description: The requested precomputed time report row used by organization reporting features.

parameters.description: The time report row identifier (UUID, global scope within the reporting dataset).
parameters.name: timeReportRowId

operations.description:
Browse the project budget report rows for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns a paginated view of the project budget report data used by reporting and operational review workflows. It is intended for users who can view organization reports and need to compare project budget hours with actual logged hours.

The result set is scoped to the active organization context. Only projects that have budget hours defined should appear in the report. Pagination and any supported report filters must be preserved across page navigation, and requests that do not match the available reporting permissions must be rejected.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_project_budget_report_rows as a report source for the current organization context.
Apply pagination and optional sorting in the request body.
Filter by the organization selected in the authenticated context; do not accept cross-organization access.
Exclude projects whose budget hours are null or otherwise not defined, because those rows are not part of the report.
Return each row with project identity, budget hours, actual hours, and budget utilization metrics as defined by the report row schema.
Validate report-view permission before querying.
If the request includes filters not supported by the report row schema, reject the request rather than widening the query.
Use a read-only query path and avoid any mutation.

responseBody.description: Paginated project budget report row summaries for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Report browsing criteria for the project budget report, including pagination and supported filters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project budget report row.

This endpoint returns one precomputed reporting row that summarizes a project's budgeted hours, actual logged hours, utilization percentage, and billable versus non-billable breakdown for a specific reporting period. The row is part of the organization's reporting data and is intended for dashboard and report detail views rather than direct editing.
