The response is scoped to the currently selected organization and the requested report row identifier. The referenced row is linked to a project and includes the report date, period start and end dates, budget hours, actual hours, utilization percentage, and billable/non-billable hour totals. Consumers should use this endpoint when they need the full metric set for a single project budget report entry.

If the report row does not exist in the current organization context, the request must fail with a not-found response. Access must also respect report viewing permissions, because this data is part of the organization's reporting surface.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project budget report row by primary key from erp_hrm_time_project_budget_report_rows.
Validate that the row belongs to the caller's selected organization context before returning it.
Join to the project only if the implementation needs to enforce organization scope or to hydrate related identifiers; do not expose unrelated project fields unless the shared response schema requires them.
Return a single full reporting row including id, organization_id, project_id, report_date, period_start_date, period_end_date, budget_hours, actual_hours, utilization_percent, billable_hours, and non_billable_hours.
Reject access when the caller lacks report viewing permission or when the row is outside the active organization. Return not found when the id does not resolve in scope. This is a derived read-only reporting projection, so no persistence changes are performed.

responseBody.description: A single project budget report row with budget, actual, utilization, and billable breakdown metrics.

parameters.description: Identifier of the project budget report row in the current organization scope.
parameters.name: projectBudgetReportRowId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated weekly summary report for the selected organization.

This report presents week-by-week time activity across a requested date range and is intended for operational review, trend analysis, and dashboard support. It returns precomputed weekly summary rows rather than raw timelog records, which keeps reporting efficient while preserving organization-level isolation.

The report is scoped to the current organization context and may be filtered by project when needed. It is designed for users who have permission to view organization reports and should reject access when the caller cannot view the underlying report data set or when the organization context is missing.

The response is suitable for summary dashboards and reporting screens that need weekly totals, counts, and other aggregated values without loading the underlying timelogs directly.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read weekly summary report rows from erp_hrm_time_weekly_summary_report_rows for the current organization context.
Apply report filters from the request body, including the date range required for the weekly summary and any optional project filter supported by the report. Group the result by week boundary as stored in the report row data and return only rows that belong to the selected organization.

Use pagination and sorting consistently with list endpoints. If the request asks for a date range outside available data, return an empty page rather than an error. Reject the request when the caller lacks report-view permission or when no organization context is selected.

Do not query raw timelog records for this endpoint unless needed to reconcile precomputed report rows; the endpoint should primarily serve from the weekly summary report table. Preserve organization isolation in every filter and join.

responseBody.description: Paginated weekly summary report rows for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Weekly summary report criteria, including date range and optional project filter.

operations.description:
Retrieve a weekly summary report row for a specific organization and week.

This endpoint returns a single precomputed reporting row that summarizes one organization’s activity for one week. The row stores the organization reference, the week start and end dates, total hours, timelog count, and the number of active employees who logged time during that week. It is intended for reporting and dashboard consumption rather than transactional editing.

The returned data reflects a derived projection used to speed up weekly reporting queries. Because the row is organization-scoped, the request must be evaluated in the caller’s selected organization context. If the row does not belong to the current organization or does not exist, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or access-denied error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the weekly summary report row by its UUID primary key and verify that the row belongs to the currently selected organization context before returning it.
Use a single indexed lookup on the reporting table. Include the related organization only if the response schema requires it; otherwise return the row entity fields directly.

Do not allow cross-organization access. If the record is missing or belongs to another organization, return not found or forbidden according to the service’s authorization conventions. This endpoint is read-only and must not mutate the derived reporting table.

responseBody.description: The weekly summary report row for the requested organization and week.

parameters.description: Weekly summary report row identifier (UUID primary key).
parameters.name: weeklySummaryReportRowId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated organization dashboard summary for the currently selected organization.

This report provides an operational overview for users with report viewing permission. It summarizes active employee count, weekly logged hours, pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects with high budget utilization, and the top employees by hours logged in the selected time range.

The data is strictly scoped to the current organization context and must never include records from other organizations. The response is intended for dashboard presentation and should reflect the organization’s precomputed summary data when available, falling back to report aggregation logic only when necessary.

If the user does not have permission to view reports in the selected organization, the request must be rejected. If the requested filters do not match any available records, return an empty result rather than expanding beyond the requested scope.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read the organization dashboard summary for the active organization context only.
Use the current organization from the authenticated member session and reject the request if no organization is selected or if the caller lacks report viewing permission.

Apply the request body filters to the organization-level dashboard data, including date range and any supported dashboard criteria defined by the summary DTO. Prefer the precomputed erp_hrm_time_organization_dashboard_summaries table as the source of truth because this model is a derived snapshot for dashboard usage. If the snapshot is missing or stale, the service may recompute the metrics from employees, timelogs, timesheets, projects, and budget data within the same organization boundary.

Enforce organization isolation in all joins and aggregations. Do not leak cross-organization values. Validate all date inputs and ensure the response shape matches the paginated summary DTO. If the user is unauthorized, return a forbidden error. If the organization context is missing, return a conflict or unauthorized error according to the platform’s auth conventions.

responseBody.description: Paginated organization dashboard summary for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Report criteria for the organization dashboard summary.

operations.description:
Retrieve a precomputed organization dashboard summary for the selected organization.

This endpoint returns a single dashboard snapshot row that stores cached operational metrics for an organization, including active employee count, pending timesheet count, weekly logged hours, and the number of projects whose budget utilization exceeds the dashboard threshold. It may also include a featured budget-risk project with cached budget and actual hour values when one is available.

The summary is organization-scoped and must be accessed within the caller's currently selected organization context. It is intended for report viewers and dashboard screens that need fast organization overview data without recalculating aggregates on every request. If the snapshot cannot be found for the requested identifier or does not belong to the selected organization, the request must be rejected with the appropriate not-found or access-control error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization dashboard summary row by its UUID primary key.
Verify the row belongs to the caller's selected organization before returning it; do not allow cross-organization access.
Use a single indexed lookup on erp_hrm_time_organization_dashboard_summaries.id, and include the organization relation only if the response serializer requires it; otherwise return the snapshot row fields directly.
Treat deleted_at as an invalidated snapshot marker if the service layer filters inactive snapshots; do not return invalidated rows when the domain rules require active data only.
If the row is missing or organization-scoped access fails, return a not-found or forbidden response consistent with the application's error policy.

responseBody.description: The organization dashboard summary snapshot for the selected organization.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization dashboard summary snapshot (UUID).
parameters.name: organizationDashboardSummaryId

operations.description:
Retrieve the current employee dashboard summary for the selected organization context.

This operation returns a precomputed snapshot of the employee’s personal dashboard, including hours logged today, hours logged this week, whether an active timer exists, the start time of that timer, the count of recent timelogs, the pending timesheet status for the active week, and counts of open and in-progress assigned tasks.

The summary is organization-scoped and reflects the currently selected member context. Consumers should use it to render the personal dashboard efficiently without assembling the data from individual timelogs, timers, timesheets, and task queries. If the snapshot is unavailable or stale, the service should resolve it from the source records and return the latest derived state.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the employee dashboard summary projection for the authenticated member within the selected organization context.
Use the unique employee identity for the current context to locate the single dashboard summary record from erp_hrm_time_employee_dashboard_summaries.
Return the record if present; if the projection has been logically invalidated or missing, rebuild the snapshot from the underlying employee, timelog, timer, timesheet, and task data sources used by the dashboard materialization process.

Do not expose data from other organizations or other employees. Validate that the current member is associated with the selected organization and that the resolved employee record belongs to that organization.
If the employee dashboard summary record cannot be found, return a not-found style error for the dashboard scope rather than fabricating default values.

Because this is a reporting projection, preserve the stored snapshot timestamps and derived counts as returned by the database. Do not mutate the projection in this read operation.

responseBody.description: A paginated set of employee dashboard summary records for the selected organization context.

requestBody.description: Dashboard retrieval criteria for the current member and organization context.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current employee dashboard summary for the authenticated member in the selected organization.

This endpoint provides the personal dashboard data used to show today’s hours, weekly hours, active timer status, recent timelogs, pending timesheet status, and the employee’s assigned work items. The response is scoped to the current organization context and reflects only the caller’s accessible employee data.

The summary is backed by the employee dashboard summary snapshot data model and is intended for fast dashboard rendering. If the employee context cannot be resolved, or if the caller does not have access to the selected organization, the request is rejected. The returned data should be treated as a current snapshot rather than a historical report.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the employee dashboard summary snapshot for the authenticated member in the current organization context. Resolve the target employee from the caller's selected organization context; do not accept a path parameter because this endpoint is not scoped to another employee.

Read from erp_hrm_time_employee_dashboard_summaries and join the employee context needed to verify access. Return the precomputed summary record that aggregates the employee's personal time-tracking and workload metrics used by the dashboard UI.

Enforce organization isolation strictly. Reject the request if the member has no selected organization, if the employee record is not accessible in that organization, or if the caller is not allowed to view the dashboard summary. If the snapshot is missing, return a not-found style error rather than constructing a partial result.

responseBody.description: The personal dashboard summary for the current employee in the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of organization activity log entries.

Activity log entries are read-only historical records that capture significant actions performed within the organization. Each entry represents a recorded event with a timestamp, the user who performed the action, the action type, the target entity, and supporting details so the organization can review what happened over time.

Use this endpoint to browse the audit trail for supported business events such as employee invitations, employee deactivations and reactivations, contract creation or editing, project creation and lifecycle changes, task status changes, timesheet submission and review decisions, and role assignment changes. Results are scoped to the currently selected organization and should be paginated, filterable, and sortable for administrative review.

This operation is read-only. Clients can search and inspect entries, but they cannot create, edit, or remove log records through this endpoint. If a requested filter returns no records, the response should still return a valid empty page. Access should be restricted to users with permission to view the organization activity log, and the implementation must enforce organization isolation on every query.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement this as a PATCH-based search endpoint over erp_hrm_time_activity_log_entries.

Accept a request body carrying pagination, sort, and filter criteria. Support filtering by action type, user, and date range, and ensure all queries are constrained to the active organization context. Build the list from the activity log table ordered by newest entries first unless an explicit sort is supplied.

Return a paginated page of summary records rather than full mutable entities, because the records are display-oriented and read-only. Include the fields needed to render the audit list: timestamp, actor, action type, target reference, and details. If the implementation joins user display data or target labels from related tables, do so read-only and never cross organization boundaries.

Reject requests from unauthorized users, and reject requests that attempt to filter or sort by unsupported fields. If the date range is invalid, return a validation error. If no matching rows are found, return an empty page with correct pagination metadata. Do not allow any write behavior for this resource.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of activity log entry summaries for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Pagination, sorting, and filter criteria for browsing organization activity log entries.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single activity log entry for the currently selected organization.

Activity log entries are read-only historical records that capture significant organization events, including the time of the action, the user who performed it, the action type, the affected target entity, and the associated details. This endpoint returns the full entry so authorized users can review the business history of the organization and understand what changed, when it changed, and who performed the action.

Access to the full activity log is limited to users with organization management permission for the current organization. The entry must belong to that organization, and the request must not expose entries from any other tenant. If the entry does not exist in the selected organization or the user lacks permission, the request must be rejected with an appropriate authorization or not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the activity_log_entries row by activityLogEntryId within the active organization context.
Enforce organization scoping before returning data so entries from other tenants cannot be accessed.
Verify the caller has organization management permission.
Return a single entity projection containing the stored entry fields required by the ActivityLogEntry model, including timestamp, performed-by user reference, action type, target entity reference, and details.
Do not allow any mutation logic. If the entry is absent in the selected organization, return not found. If the caller lacks permission, return forbidden.
If the schema exposes foreign-key relations to users or target entities, populate them only as read-only references; do not infer or synthesize missing linked records.

responseBody.description: The full activity log entry for the selected organization.

parameters.description: The activity log entry identifier within the selected organization (global identifier).
parameters.name: activityLogEntryId

operations.description:
Transfers ownership of an organization to another eligible member of the same organization.

This operation is used when the current owner needs to hand over control before deleting an account or changing organizational responsibility. The target owner must already belong to the organization, and the transfer must preserve the organization record while updating its ownership reference.

The request is validated against organization membership boundaries and ownership constraints. If the current user is not allowed to manage ownership, if the target member does not exist in the organization, or if the organization cannot accept the transfer due to business rules, the request must be rejected with a clear error response. The organization remains the same tenant boundary after the transfer, but future ownership-based actions will use the new owner.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the organization by organizationId and verify it exists in the current selected organization context.
Verify the authenticated member has authority to transfer ownership for this organization, typically the current owner or a user with organization management permission.
Validate that the requested new owner is an active organization member and is not blocked by membership status.
Perform the ownership change in a transaction: update the organization ownership reference to the target member, and if the schema tracks ownership-related membership flags or context selection, ensure they remain consistent after the move.
Emit an activity log entry for ownership transfer if the system records organization-level actions.
Reject the request when the organization does not exist, the target member is not in the organization, the requester lacks permission, or the transfer would violate ownership rules. Return a conflict or validation error when the target member is invalid for ownership.

responseBody.description: The organization after ownership has been transferred to the new owner.

parameters.description: Identifier of the organization whose ownership will be transferred.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Ownership transfer request containing the organization member who will become the new owner.

prerequisites.description: An organization record must exist before its ownership can be transferred to another eligible member.

operations.description:
Create an employee invitation for the currently selected organization.

This operation lets a user with employee management permission invite someone to work in the organization by email. If the email already belongs to an existing account, the system attaches that account to the organization immediately. If the email does not yet belong to an account, the system creates a pending invitation that will be resolved automatically when the person signs up with the same email address.

The invitation is always scoped to the active organization context and does not affect memberships in other organizations. The request is rejected when the caller lacks the required permission, when the email cannot be used for invitation matching, or when the organization already has the relevant association for that email.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated member has employee management permission in the current organization context.
Resolve the active organization from the session/context; do not accept organization identifiers in the request body.
Validate the submitted email address and reject malformed or non-matchable values.
Check whether a member account already exists for the email. If it exists, create or reuse the organization membership/employee linkage according to the existing onboarding flow and avoid duplicates. If no account exists, create a pending invitation record for this organization and email, ensuring repeated invitations do not create duplicate pending entries for the same organization-email pair.
Return the resulting invitation/attachment record in a shape consistent with the organization-scoped invitation workflow. Record any required activity log entry if invitation creation is audited elsewhere in the service.
Handle concurrency by enforcing uniqueness on the organization-email combination where applicable and mapping conflicts to a validation/business error rather than duplicating records.

responseBody.description: The recorded invitation result for the organization, including whether the email was attached to an existing account or stored as a pending invitation.

requestBody.description: Invitation details for a new employee invite in the current organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of employee invitations for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is used by authorized members to review employee onboarding invitations within the active organization. It shows invitation records associated with email-based employee setup so managers can see which invitations are pending, which have already connected to an account, and which are ready to be acted on in the current tenant context.

Access is limited to callers with employee management permission in the selected organization. The response must remain strictly organization-scoped and should only return summary data suitable for browsing and administrative review. Records from other organizations must never be exposed through this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the organization-scoped invitation source for the active organization only.
Apply employee-management authorization before loading any data.
Return a paginated result set ordered by newest invitation first, and support standard list filtering/search/sorting in the request DTO if available downstream.
Ensure the query is constrained to the authenticated member's selected organization context.
If invitation data is modeled indirectly through membership or employee attachment records, compose a stable summary view from the authoritative rows that represent invitation status and email target, and deduplicate by organization/email target as needed.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of employee invitation summaries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for employee invitations in the active organization.

operations.description:
Deactivate an employee within the current organization.

This operation stops an employee from actively participating in the organization while preserving their historical timelogs and timesheets. It is intended for access removal and staff lifecycle management, and it records the change as an activity log entry for organizational auditing.

The employee must belong to the current organization context, and the caller must have permission to manage employees. The system rejects the request if the employee is already deactivated or if the target cannot be modified in the selected organization.
operations.name: deactivateEmployee
operations.specification:
Load the employee by employeeId within the current organization context and verify the caller has employee management permission. Reject with not found if the employee does not belong to the organization or cannot be accessed in the current context.

Validate that the employee is currently active. If the employee is already deactivated, return a conflict or validation error without changing state.

Update the employee status to deactivated in a single transactional operation. Preserve all existing timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and other historical records. Do not delete or detach historical time data.

After the employee status change, create an activity log entry describing the deactivation action, including the action type, timestamp, actor, affected employee, and change details. If activity logging fails, roll back the employee status change so the deactivation remains consistent.

Return the updated employee entity after the transaction commits.

responseBody.description: The updated employee record after deactivation.

parameters.description: The employee identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Reactivate a deactivated employee and restore active participation in the organization.

This operation changes the employee record from deactivated back to active for the currently selected organization. It is intended for organization members with employee management privileges who need to restore access for someone whose employment or access pause has ended. The employee remains the same record, and the operation does not create a new employee entry.

Reactivation preserves the employee's historical records, including prior timelogs and timesheets. After reactivation, the employee can again log time and submit timesheets according to the organization rules. The system also records an activity log entry describing the reactivation event, including the acting user, the affected employee, the action timestamp, and related details.

If the employee does not exist in the current organization, is already active, or the caller lacks the required permission, the request must be rejected with an appropriate error response.
operations.name: reactivate
operations.specification:
Load the employee by id within the current organization scope. Verify the authenticated member has employee management permission. Confirm the employee belongs to the current organization and is currently deactivated; if not found or already active, return a domain error.

Update the employee status to active and persist the change in a single transaction. Do not alter historical timelogs, timesheets, contracts, or other preserved records. After the employee status update succeeds, insert an activity log entry in erp_hrm_time_activity_log_entries using the current organization id, acting member id, action type for employee reactivation, the employee id as the target entity, and a human-readable details message.

If there are related permission or state checks that fail, abort without writing either the employee update or the activity log entry. Return the updated employee entity after reload so the client receives the current state. Use the existing employee schema fields only; do not assume any additional status or audit columns beyond those provided.

responseBody.description: The reactivated employee record after the status change is applied.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the employee to reactivate within the current organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Retrieve the paginated historical contract timeline for an employee.

This operation returns the sequence of employment contracts that define how the employee’s pay rate, pay period, working hours, and notes changed over time. Contracts are preserved as historical records, so the response is intended for review and auditing rather than editing.

The history is available to the employee who owns the record and to users who have employee view permission in the organization. The service must enforce organization context and reject access when the caller is not allowed to view that employee’s contract records.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target employee within the current organization context, then query erp_hrm_time_employee_contracts for that employee's contracts ordered from earliest to latest by start date, and secondarily by end date or creation order if needed for stable sorting. Apply pagination to the result set and return contract summaries only.

Enforce access control before querying: allow the employee themselves, or any member with employee:view permission in the same organization. Reject cross-organization access. Because the endpoint is for history, do not allow create, update, or delete behavior here.

The response should preserve the contract timeline exactly as stored, including ongoing contracts with a null end date. If an employee has no contracts, return an empty page rather than an error. Use only the contract fields defined by the schema and do not infer hidden audit fields.

responseBody.description: Paginated employee contract history ordered by the sequence in which contracts were used.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full contract history for an employee.

This operation returns the employee’s historical employment contracts in chronological order so the caller can review how pay rate, pay period, working hours, and notes changed over time. The history is an authoritative record of the employee’s employment arrangement within the selected organization, and it is scoped to a single employee rather than the global user account.

An employee may view their own contract history, and users with employee view permission may view another employee’s contracts. The returned records include both active and past contracts, preserving the sequence of contract periods without allowing the past records to be rewritten through this endpoint.

If the employee does not exist in the current organization context, or if the caller lacks permission to view the target employee’s contracts, the request must be rejected. The response should preserve the natural contract order so clients can render the timeline directly.
operations.name: history
operations.specification:
Load the employee by id within the current organization context, then verify access: allow the employee to view their own history or require employee:view permission for any other employee. Query erp_hrm_time_employee_contracts by erp_hrm_time_employee_id and sort by start_date ascending, using end_date as additional ordering if needed to keep chronology stable. Do not filter out inactive or past contracts; the whole record set is the history.

Map each contract using only actual columns from the schema: id, erp_hrm_time_employee_id, start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at if the downstream DTO includes it. Preserve null end_date for ongoing contracts. Return a history-shaped payload suitable for display as an ordered list; do not allow modifications here.

Handle missing employee, cross-organization access, and permission denial as standard not found or forbidden outcomes according to the service conventions. Because contract history is read-only and must remain immutable, this endpoint must never perform writes or derived updates.

responseBody.description: Ordered employee contract history for the selected employee.

parameters.description: Employee identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Check whether a role can be deleted in the current organization.

This operation validates the target role against the organization role rules and returns a deletion eligibility result for use in role management screens. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are permanently protected and must always be reported as non-deletable. Custom roles may be deleted only when no employees are assigned to them.

The check is scoped to the selected organization context and must not cross tenant boundaries. If the role does not exist in the current organization, the request should fail with a not-found response. If the role is protected or still referenced by employees, the response should explain the blocking condition so the caller can present a clear message before attempting deletion.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the role by id within the current organization context.
Verify that the role belongs to the selected organization and reject cross-organization access.
Evaluate delete eligibility using role rules: built-in roles are always blocked, and custom roles are deletable only when no employee records reference them.
The check should count or query employee assignments against the role to determine whether the role is in use.
Return a dedicated deletion-check DTO containing the eligibility flag and human-readable blocker reason(s). Do not modify any data.
If the role id is not found in the organization, return a not-found error. If the role is already deleted by the underlying persistence layer, treat it as not found.

responseBody.description: Deletion eligibility result for a role in the current organization.

parameters.description: Role identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Get the effective permission set for a role.

This operation returns the permissions that are actually available to the selected role within its organization. It is intended for role management screens and authorization-aware clients that need to display or evaluate what a role can do, based on the approved permission catalog and the role’s assigned permission rows.

The role belongs to exactly one organization and is identified by its role record. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are protected by business rules, while custom roles may be configured through approved permissions only. The response should reflect the permission keys and their human-readable descriptions as defined in the permission catalog, without inventing any additional permission values.

If the role does not exist in the current organization context, the request must fail with a not-found error. If the caller lacks permission to view role data in the selected organization, the request must fail with an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the role by id within the currently selected organization context and verify that it belongs to that organization. Join role_permissions to permissions and return the effective permission list as approved catalog entries.

Do not return deleted or inactive permission rows. Preserve the catalog ordering only if the domain layer defines one; otherwise sort deterministically by permission key. For built-in roles, compute the visible effective permissions from the stored role-permission assignments and do not assume any implicit permissions beyond the configured data unless the domain rules explicitly provide them.

Enforce access control using the selected organization context and the caller’s permissions. Return 404 when the role is not found in scope, and return 403 when the caller cannot view role/authorization data. No request body is required.

responseBody.description: Effective permissions for the requested role, including approved permission keys and their descriptions.

parameters.description: Role identifier within the selected organization.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Retrieve the paginated task status history for a project.

This endpoint returns the immutable audit trail of task status changes recorded for tasks that belong to the specified project. Each entry includes the task, the member who made the change, the previous status, the new status, and the exact timestamp of the transition. It is intended for project-level review so users can trace how work moved through the workflow over time.

The results are scoped to the currently selected organization and only include history rows for tasks within the requested project. Access should follow the project's view permissions, and the service must reject requests that fall outside the caller's organization or authorization scope. Because task history entries are append-only records, this operation is strictly read-only and does not support modification.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the project by id within the current organization scope and verify project-view access before querying history. Resolve task history through erp_hrm_time_task_history_entries joined to erp_hrm_time_tasks, filtering only tasks whose erp_hrm_time_project_id matches the requested project. Return paginated results ordered by changed_at descending, with a stable secondary order by id to keep pagination consistent.

Do not cross organization boundaries in any join or filter. If the project does not exist in the current organization, return not found. If the caller lacks access, return forbidden or the application's standard access-denied response. The endpoint is read-only and must never expose update or delete behavior.

responseBody.description: Paginated task status history entries for the specified project.

parameters.description: Project identifier within the currently selected organization.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Pagination and filtering criteria for project task history browsing.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full status-change history for a task within a project.

This operation returns the recorded lifecycle trail for the selected task, showing each historical change in chronological order. It is intended for accountability and review, allowing users to see when the task moved from one status to another and who performed the change.

The task history is an immutable audit-style record. Each entry belongs to exactly one task and one project scope, and the returned data must not include entries from other tasks or other projects. If the task does not exist, does not belong to the specified project, or is not visible in the current organization context, the request should fail with a not-found or access-related error as appropriate.

Because the history is append-only, this endpoint only reads the stored trail and does not allow editing or deletion of historical entries.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project and task by the supplied identifiers and verify that the task belongs to the project and current organization context before querying history.

Query erp_hrm_time_task_history_entries filtered by the task reference, ordered by recorded timestamp ascending so the consumer can reconstruct the lifecycle sequence. Return all immutable history entries for the task, including the old status, new status, timestamp, and actor responsible for the change.

Do not join or expose unrelated task records. Do not allow any mutation behavior in this endpoint. If the project or task cannot be resolved within the current tenant scope, return a not-found response. If the caller lacks permission to view the project/task, return the standard authorization error for the service.

responseBody.description: The ordered task history trail for the selected task.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project that owns the task.
parameters.name: projectId

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the task whose history is being retrieved.
parameters.name: taskId

operations.description:
Start a live timer for the current employee.

This operation creates a running time-tracking session tied to the selected project in the current organization. The timer captures the work context from the beginning, including the optional task and a short description of the work being performed, so the session can later be stopped and converted into a timelog.

The selected project must belong to the current organization, and any provided task must belong to that project. The system also enforces that each employee can have only one active timer at a time, and deactivated employees cannot start a timer. If validation fails, the request is rejected and no running session is created.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new running timer for the authenticated member's employee in the current organization.

Resolve the employee from the authenticated member and selected organization context, then verify the employee is active. Reject the request if the employee has an existing active timer because only one timer may run per employee. Verify the target project exists in the same organization and is eligible for timer tracking. If taskId is supplied, verify the task exists, belongs to the same project, and belongs to the same organization through the project relationship.

Insert a new erp_hrm_time_timers row with member_id, employee_id, project_id, optional task_id, started_at, description, created_at, and updated_at. started_at must be the current timestamp. Do not create any timelog here; timelog creation happens only when the timer is stopped. Return the created timer record with its relations as needed by the Timer response schema.

Handle conflicts and invalid references explicitly: active timer conflict, inactive employee, missing project, project/task scope mismatch, and organization scope mismatch. Because this is a create operation, use standard transactional behavior to ensure no duplicate active timer is inserted under concurrent requests.

responseBody.description: The newly started running timer session.

requestBody.description: Timer start data for the current employee.

prerequisites.description: A timer can only start against an existing project in the current organization, so the project must be created before the timer can reference it.

operations.description:
Stop the currently running timer and convert it into a completed timelog.

This operation ends the employee’s active live work session in the currently selected organization. When the timer is stopped, the system calculates the elapsed duration, rounds it to the nearest minute, and creates a timelog that preserves the timer’s work context, including the recorded start timestamp, project, task, and description.

The endpoint is part of the time-tracking workflow for members who are actively tracking work in real time. It enforces organization isolation and employee activity status, so requests are rejected when the caller has no active timer, the timer belongs to another organization, or the employee is deactivated. If the timer cannot be stopped for business reasons, the service must return a validation or conflict error instead of creating a timelog.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
Resolve the caller’s current organization context and active employee identity from the authenticated session.
Load the active timer for that employee within the selected organization only. If no active timer exists, return a conflict or not-found style error consistent with the service conventions.

Before stopping, verify the employee is still active and that the timer belongs to the current organization. Reject the request if the timer is outside scope or the employee is deactivated.

Compute the elapsed duration from the timer’s start timestamp to the stop moment, round the result to the nearest minute, and persist a new timelog using the timer’s stored work context. The created timelog must inherit the timer’s project, optional task, and description, and it should capture the timer’s start timestamp as the beginning of the work session.

Perform the timer stop and timelog creation atomically in a transaction so partial updates cannot occur. After successful creation, mark the timer as stopped/consumed according to the existing persistence model and return the created timelog entity. If the timer has already been stopped concurrently, fail safely with a conflict error.

responseBody.description: The completed timelog created from the stopped timer.

operations.description:
Discard the current running timer for the active employee.

This operation ends a live time-tracking session without creating a timelog. It is intended for employees who started tracking time but decide not to convert the running session into a recorded time entry. The discarded timer is removed immediately and can no longer be edited, stopped, or resumed.

The request is evaluated in the current organization context and against the authenticated employee's own timer. The system rejects the action if the employee does not have an active timer, if the employee is deactivated, or if another business rule prevents timer actions in the current state. Because discarding does not produce a timelog, no reporting or timesheet data is generated from the discarded session.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member's employee record in the selected organization context, then fetch the employee's currently active timer. If no active timer exists, return a not-found or conflict-style error consistent with timer workflows.

Before deleting, verify the employee is active. If the employee has been deactivated, block the request.

Perform a transactional delete of the timer row only. Do not create a timelog, do not update timesheets, and do not emit any duration calculation. This endpoint must not affect other timers because the domain allows only one active timer per employee.

Apply organization isolation so the employee can only discard a timer inside the current selected organization. If the timer belongs to a different organization context, reject the request. After deletion, return success with no body.

operations.description:
Retrieve the timer that is currently running for the authenticated employee.

This endpoint lets a member confirm whether live time tracking is active in the current organization context and inspect the running session details, including its associated project, optional task, description, and start time.

If the employee has no active timer, the request should be handled as a read of an absent current timer according to the service’s standard not-found behavior for singleton resources. The endpoint only exposes the timer for the currently authenticated member and does not allow access to other employees’ running sessions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated member and current organization context from the request. Resolve the active timer for that employee by querying erp_hrm_time_timers for the row whose employee ownership matches the current member and whose running state indicates it is active.

Return the full timer entity with its current project, optional task, start timestamp, and description fields. Do not create, modify, or stop the timer in this operation. If no active timer exists for the employee, respond with the service’s standard 404/not-found handling for singleton current-resource reads.

Enforce organization isolation through the current context before querying. Ensure the response never leaks another employee’s timer. Since this is a read-only singleton endpoint, there is no pagination, filtering, or request body.

responseBody.description: The currently running timer for the authenticated employee.

operations.description:
Create a draft timesheet for a specific week.

This operation creates the editable weekly timesheet record for the currently selected organization and authenticated employee. When the draft is created, the system automatically includes all timelogs for that employee that fall within the selected week, so the employee can review and adjust the weekly record before submission.

A draft timesheet belongs to exactly one employee and one Monday-to-Sunday week. The created record remains in draft status until it is submitted for approval. If another timesheet already exists for the same employee and week, the request must fail to preserve the one-timesheet-per-week rule. The service must also ensure the target week is valid and that the employee is allowed to manage their own timesheet within the current organization context.

If the employee has no timelogs in the selected week, the draft may still be created if the business workflow allows it for later manual addition; however, submission will remain blocked until at least one timelog is included. Any validation error such as an invalid week boundary or duplicate weekly timesheet should be returned clearly to the client.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member and the currently selected organization, then resolve the employee record that owns timesheets in that organization. Validate that the requested week start date is a Monday and compute the matching week end date as Sunday of the same week.

Check for an existing non-deleted timesheet for the same employee and week_start_date using the unique constraint on erp_hrm_time_timesheets. If one exists, reject the request with a conflict error. Create the timesheet row with status draft and null submitted_at, reviewed_at, reviewed_by_member_id, and rejection_reason. Persist the row first, then fetch all timelogs for the employee whose work_date falls within the week range and create join rows in erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs for each matching timelog, avoiding duplicates through the unique constraint on the join table.

Run the create and join-row inserts in a transaction so the draft and its included timelogs stay consistent. Scope all queries to the current organization through the employee relation, and ensure only the current employee's own timesheets can be created. Return the created timesheet entity with its identifiers and current lifecycle fields. Do not attempt to modify locked approved timesheets or existing submitted/reviewed records, and do not create duplicate join rows if the draft is regenerated in an idempotent retry scenario.

responseBody.description: The created draft timesheet with its current lifecycle state and weekly ownership metadata.

requestBody.description: Draft timesheet creation payload containing the target week for the currently selected employee.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for approval.

This operation changes a weekly timesheet from draft to submitted so it can be reviewed by users with approval permission. The timesheet remains owned by the same employee and tied to the same weekly period after submission.

Only the employee who owns the timesheet, or a user with approval permissions in the selected organization context, may perform this action according to the organization’s access rules. The service must reject submissions for locked, already submitted, approved, or otherwise invalid timesheets, and it must preserve the timesheet’s existing timelogs and week boundaries when the status changes.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id within the current organization context and verify that it belongs to the active organization. Confirm the requester is either the timesheet owner or has the appropriate approval/management permission required by the domain rules.

Validate that the timesheet is currently in draft status. Reject the request if it is already submitted, approved, or otherwise not editable. Reject if the timesheet has no included timelogs, because submission requires at least one timelog. Reject if the employee is deactivated, because deactivated employees cannot submit timesheets.

When valid, update the timesheet status from draft to submitted and set the submitted timestamp to the current time. Preserve the week start/end dates, owner, and existing timelog links. If the implementation stores submission metadata on the timesheet, persist it in the same transaction. The operation should be idempotent only in the sense that a repeated submit on a non-draft timesheet must fail with a domain validation error rather than silently reapplying the transition.

Return the updated timesheet entity after commit. Use transactional integrity so that status changes and any related submission metadata are written atomically. Surface not-found, forbidden, and domain validation failures with appropriate HTTP errors.

responseBody.description: The submitted timesheet after its status changes to submitted.

parameters.description: The timesheet identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A weekly timesheet draft must exist before it can be submitted for approval.

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet for the current organization.

This operation is available only to users with timesheet approval permission. It finalizes a weekly timesheet that is already in submitted status and returns the approved record so the client can refresh the reviewer-facing view.

After approval, the included timelogs are locked because the weekly time record is finalized. Requests must be rejected when the timesheet is not submitted, belongs to a different organization, or the caller does not have approval permission.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by ID within the authenticated member's selected organization. Verify that the caller has the time approval permission and that the timesheet status is submitted. Reject the request with a forbidden or conflict-style error if the user lacks permission, the timesheet is outside the current organization, or the status is not submitted.

On success, update the timesheet status from submitted to approved and persist the review timestamp and reviewer reference if those fields exist in the schema. Then lock all timelogs associated with the timesheet through the join table so they cannot be edited or deleted afterward. Perform the status update and locking in a transaction to avoid partial approval states. Return the refreshed timesheet entity after the update.

If the data model includes a dedicated relation for reviewed-by or reviewed-at, populate it from the current member context and current timestamp. If the schema does not expose review metadata fields, only change the status and apply the locking side effects defined by the timesheet-timelog relationship.

responseBody.description: The approved timesheet after the approval action has been applied.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet to approve within the current organization.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet with a required reason.

This operation is used by an approver to review a submitted weekly timesheet and send it back to the employee for correction. A rejection is only valid when the timesheet is currently in submitted status and belongs to the selected organization context. The rejection reason is mandatory so the employee understands what must be fixed before resubmission.

When the rejection is accepted, the timesheet returns to draft status and remains editable by its owner. The reviewed timestamp and reviewer reference are updated as part of the review workflow, and the included timelogs remain associated with the same weekly timesheet so the employee can revise and resubmit it. Requests for draft, approved, or already rejected timesheets must be rejected.

Access is limited to users with timesheet approval permission. If the user lacks permission, if the timesheet is outside the current organization, or if the target timesheet is not eligible for rejection, the request must fail with an appropriate validation or authorization error.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by ID within the current organization scope. Verify that the authenticated member has approval permission. Reject the request if the timesheet does not belong to the active organization, if it is not in submitted status, or if it is already approved or rejected.

Validate the request body to require a non-empty rejection reason. Persist the status transition from submitted to draft and store the reviewer/review metadata according to the timesheet schema. Keep the included timelogs linked to the timesheet; do not remove them during rejection.

The operation should be transactional so that status, review metadata, and any related audit/event side effects are saved together. Return the updated timesheet entity after persistence. If the record is missing, return not found. If the status is not eligible, return a domain validation error.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet after rejection, returned in draft status with review metadata applied.

parameters.description: The timesheet identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Rejection payload containing the mandatory reason for returning the timesheet to draft.

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitor who can sign up, log in, and join the platform through invitations or pending organization access.

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated user who works within one or more selected organizations and can perform actions based on the organization role and permissions assigned to the user.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.
